````text
1	---
2	name: python-project-best-practice
3	description: 'Modern Python project conventions for the agentic-coding era: uv + src layout, Tyro CLIs with shell completion, marimo notebooks that run as scripts, loguru, and ruff/type/pytest gates behind a Justfile, plus an AGENTS.md contract agents can drive. Use when starting a new Python project or package, scaffolding a pyproject.toml, choosing a CLI/test/lint/logging stack, making a tool installable with `uv tool install`, or modernizing a legacy setup.py / requirements.txt / poetry / conda repo.'
4	---
5	
6	# Python Project Best Practice
7	
8	An opinionated baseline for Python projects that both people and agents work
9	in. Two entry points: scaffold a new project (Workflow A), or score and
10	modernize an existing one (Workflow B). The same conventions drive both.
11	
12	The bias throughout: **every operation has one canonical, discoverable,
13	non-interactive command**. That is what makes a project workable by an agent,
14	and it happens to be what makes it pleasant for humans.
15	
16	## When to use
17	
18	- "Start a new Python project / package / CLI tool"
19	- "Set up pyproject.toml", "which should I use, uv or poetry / pip-tools?"
20	- "How do I make this installable so someone can just run it?"
21	- "Modernize this repo" — setup.py, requirements.txt, poetry, conda, flat layout
22	- Choosing between ruff/black, mypy/ty, extras/dependency-groups, just/taskipy
23	- Adding a CLI, notebooks, an HTTP surface, or a Rust extension to a Python repo
24	
25	## When NOT to use
26	
27	These skills own their territory. Delegate rather than restate:
28	
29	| Topic | Skill |
30	|---|---|
31	| `--help` / `--dry-run` / `--print-config` / exit-code design and verification | `verifiable-surfaces` |
32	| marimo dual-mode notebooks, sweeps, tracking | `marimo-batch-mlflow`; format rules in `marimo-notebook`; widgets in `anywidget` |
33	| Production FastAPI internals | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
34	| Docs site, GitHub Pages, llms.txt | `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` |
35	| Releasing a compiled Go/Rust binary | `cli-release-distribution` (Python distribution stays here) |
36	| pre-commit setup, secret remediation | `agent-history-hygiene` |
37	| TDD discipline itself | `engineering-fundamentals/tdd` |
38	| Building an MCP server | `mcp-builder` (read `references/api-and-services.md` first — usually you want a subcommand) |
39	
40	Also not for: a one-file script (use a PEP 723 header and stop), or a
41	maintenance-only repo where a migration buys nothing.
42	
43	## Authoritative sources
44	
45	Fetch the page rather than guessing — this toolchain moves fast, and several
46	of these projects change CLI surface between minor versions.
47	
48	| Thing | Where |
49	|---|---|
50	| uv | <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/> · CLI reference <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/> |
51	| ruff rules | <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/> |
52	| ty | <https://github.com/astral-sh/ty> (0.0.x — check the version before quoting behavior) |
53	| Tyro | <https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/> · completion <https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/> |
54	| loguru | <https://loguru.readthedocs.io/> |
55	| pydantic-settings | <https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/> |
56	| PyO3 / maturin | <https://pyo3.rs/> · <https://www.maturin.rs/> |
57	| Python versions / EOL | <https://devguide.python.org/versions/> (3.10 EOL Oct 2026; default floor `>=3.11`) |
58	| Packaging specs | <https://packaging.python.org/> · PEP 735 (dependency groups), PEP 723 (script deps) |
59	
60	## The canonical layout
61	
62	```
63	pyproject.toml          [project] + [dependency-groups] + tool config. One file.
64	uv.lock                 committed. Pins YOUR dev env, never your users'.
65	.python-version         dev interpreter (uv python pin). Not the same as requires-python.
66	Justfile                every supported operation. `just --list` is the surface.
67	AGENTS.md               the agent contract. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it.
68	README.md               getting started for humans: uv sync, just check.
69	.envrc / .env.example   direnv activation; the tracked contract for .env (which is ignored).
70	
71	src/my_tool/            src layout: tests import the INSTALLED package
72	  core.py               domain logic. stdlib logging. no side effects at import.
73	  _log.py               loguru setup. called by entry points only.
74	  settings.py           pydantic-settings: defaults < .env < environment.
75	  cli/                  one frozen dataclass per subcommand; run() -> exit code
76	  py.typed              without this your annotations are invisible to consumers
77	tests/                  mirrors src/ module for module
78	scripts/                repo helpers, NOT importable from the package
79	notebooks/              marimo notebooks. import the package; nothing imports them.
80	.agents/skills/my-tool/ the package's own skill, shipped with the code
81	.github/workflows/ci.yml  runs the same gate as `just check`
82	```
83	
84	Two arrows to keep straight: `notebooks/` and `scripts/` may import the
85	package; the package imports neither.
86	
87	## Decision: which profile?
88	
89	Start at the smallest row that fits and add later — profiles are additive, so
90	"agentic later" costs nothing now.
91	
92	| Profile | Use when | Adds | Read |
93	|---|---|---|---|
94	| `minimal` | a library nobody runs from a shell yet | package, tests, Justfile, CI, AGENTS.md | `uv-and-pyproject`, `quality-gates` |
95	| `cli` **(default)** | almost everything | Tyro CLI, loguru, pydantic-settings, `[project.scripts]` | + `tyro-cli`, `logging-and-config` |
96	| `lib` | others will import it | publishing metadata, `py.typed` | + `uv-and-pyproject` §Distribution |
97	| `api` | it serves HTTP | FastAPI app, `/docs`, `/openapi.json` | + `api-and-services` |
98	| `ml` | experiments and notebooks | marimo notebook that is also a CLI | + `notebooks-and-widgets` |
99	| `rust` | a profiled, CPU-bound hot loop | maturin backend, PyO3 crate, `.pyi` stubs | + `rust-pyo3` |
100	
101	Companion skills to recommend, by profile, are in
102	[`references/agent-interface.md`](references/agent-interface.md) and in the
103	scaffolder's `recommended_skills[]`.
104	
105	## Workflow A — new project from zero
106	
107	### 1. Decide the profile, name, and Python targets
108	
109	Ask only what you cannot infer: what the project does, whether it needs a CLI,
110	HTTP, notebooks, or Rust, and whether the user has a preferred local Python
111	version for `.venv`. The slug is hyphen-case (`churn-scorer`); the package is
112	the underscore form (`churn_scorer`).
113	
114	Keep the two Python version knobs separate:
115	
116	- **`--python-pin` (`.python-version`, default `auto`)**: the local dev
117	  interpreter. `auto` detects the user's installed `3.11+` local Python so
118	  `uv sync` reuses their local interpreter and warm `uv` wheel cache instead of
119	  downloading a new Python. Pass `--python-pin 3.12` (etc.) if the user states a
120	  preference.
121	- **`--python-floor` (`requires-python`, default `3.11`)**: the package's
122	  downstream compatibility floor — set to the oldest non-EOL Python
123	  ([devguide](https://devguide.python.org/versions/): 3.10 reached EOL in Oct
124	  2026) unless the code genuinely needs `3.12+` features or must target a legacy
125	  `3.10` host. If the user's local Python is `<=3.10`, advise upgrading with
126	  `uv python install 3.13 && uv python pin 3.13`.
127	
128	### 2. Generate
129	
130	```bash
131	# preview first — writes nothing
132	uv run skills/local/python-project-best-practice/scripts/new-python-project.py \
133	    --dry-run --profile cli ./my-tool
134	
135	uv run .../new-python-project.py --profile cli --owner <gh-user> \
136	    --description "One line." ./my-tool
137	```
138	
139	JSON summary on stdout (`project`, `package`, `profile`, `files[]`,
140	`recommended_skills[]`, `next_steps[]`); progress on stderr.
141	
142	### 3. Verify it actually works
143	
144	```bash
145	cd ./my-tool
146	uv sync
147	just docs-sync     # fills the CLI block in AGENTS.md from --help
148	just check         # fmt + lint + types + tests + docs-drift
149	```
150	
151	`just check` must be green before you hand the project over. If it is not,
152	that is a bug in this skill's template — fix the template, not the generated
153	copy.
154	
155	### 4. Offer the companion skills
156	
157	Print the install line and let the user choose:
158	
159	```bash
160	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
161	```
162	
163	Do not vendor copies into the new repo — copies have no update path.
164	
165	## Workflow B — modernize an existing project
166	
167	### 1. Audit, read-only
168	
169	```bash
170	uv run skills/local/python-project-best-practice/scripts/audit-python-project.py \
171	    --format table /path/to/repo
172	```
173	
174	27 checks with evidence and a fix hint, plus an ordered `migration_plan[]`.
175	Exit `4` when something fails. It never writes, and there is deliberately no
176	`--fix`.
177	
178	### 2. Show the user the plan and agree on scope
179	
180	Nobody asked you to rewrite their build system. Confirm which rungs to do now.
181	
182	### 3. One rung per pull request
183	
184	The ladder is ordered by dependency: environment → layout → dependency
185	declaration → lint/format → types → tests → task runner + CI → console script
186	→ logging layering → agent contract → secrets. Each rung ends with the test
187	suite green.
188	
189	Read [`references/legacy-refactor.md`](references/legacy-refactor.md) before
190	the first rung. The traps that ruin these migrations — `uv add -r
191	requirements.txt` flattening the dependency graph, a formatting commit
192	destroying `git blame`, a tracked `.env` needing rotation before any history
193	rewrite — are all there.
194	
195	## Available scripts
196	
197	- **`scripts/new-python-project.py <target-dir>`** — scaffold from the bundled
198	  template tree. Offline; writes nothing outside the target.
199	  - Flags: `--profile {minimal,cli,lib,api,ml,rust}`, `--name`, `--description`,
200	    `--author`, `--owner`, `--python-floor`, `--python-pin`, `--dry-run`,
201	    `--force`, `--no-git`, `--help`.
202	  - Output: JSON on stdout, progress on stderr.
203	  - Exit: `0` ok · `2` usage · `3` target exists without `--force` ·
204	    `4` template tree and `assets/manifest.toml` disagree.
205	- **`scripts/audit-python-project.py [path]`** — read-only scorecard +
206	  migration plan.
207	  - Flags: `--format {json,table}`, `--fail-on {fail,warn,never}`, `--help`.
208	  - Exit: `0` clean · `3` path is not a directory · `4` findings at or above
209	    the threshold.
210	
211	Both are PEP 723 `uv run` scripts with inline dependencies — no environment
212	setup needed before calling them.
213	
214	## Bundled assets
215	
216	- `assets/project/` — the template tree. Every file ends `.tmpl`; the generator
217	  strips the suffix, substitutes placeholders, and drops
218	  `# __IF:profile,...__ … # __END__` blocks that the chosen profile does not
219	  want.
220	- `assets/manifest.toml` — maps each destination path to the profiles that get
221	  it. **A file not listed here is never copied**, and the generator fails
222	  (exit 4) if the manifest and the tree disagree in either direction.
223

225	
226	Load on demand — do not read them all up front.
227	
228	| File | Load when |
229	|---|---|
230	| [`uv-and-pyproject.md`](references/uv-and-pyproject.md) | writing `pyproject.toml`, lockfile policy, build backends, interpreter pinning, workspaces, publishing |
231	| [`tyro-cli.md`](references/tyro-cli.md) | building or splitting a CLI, subcommands, completion, config objects |

238	| [`legacy-refactor.md`](references/legacy-refactor.md) | Workflow B — reading the scorecard, ordering the migration |
239	
240	## Gotchas
241	
242	- **`uv sync` deletes what is not in the lock.** A manual `uv pip install`
243	  disappears on the next sync with no warning. Change dependencies with
244	  `uv add` / `uv remove` so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` move together.
245	- **Do not run black and `ruff format` together.** `ruff format` is a black
246	  reimplementation; two formatters fight over magic trailing commas and quoting
247	  and every commit reformats the last one's output. Pick ruff.
248	- **A flat layout imports your source directory, not the installed package.**
249	  Missing `__init__.py`, missing `py.typed`, unshipped package data — all [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]
250	  the test suite and break the user's install. `src/` is what closes that gap.
251	- **`[dependency-groups]` is not `[project.optional-dependencies]`.** An extra
252	  is published and installable by your users; a PEP 735 group is local-only.
253	  Your test runner in an extra is a defect you cannot remove without a release.
254	  `uv sync` installs the `dev` group by default.
255	- **`uv.lock` does not constrain your users — `[project.dependencies]` and
256	  `requires-python` do.** Installed as a dependency or via `uv tool install`,
257	  your package is resolved from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` is ignored.
258	  Commit `uv.lock` to pin *your* dev and CI environment, but keep
259	  `[project.dependencies]` floors as wide as your actual API usage allows (`>=`
260	  the lowest compatible release, no `<` or `~=` upper caps).
261	- **`uv init` and `uv add` over-constrain packages by default.** `uv init` sets
262	  `requires-python` to whatever interpreter you ran it with (e.g. `>=3.13`), and
263	  `uv add foo` writes `foo>=<version-released-today>`. If others install your
264	  package, both cause avoidable solver conflicts: lower `requires-python` to the
265	  oldest non-EOL Python your features actually need (`>=3.11`), and relax
266	  `[project.dependencies]` floors after `uv add`.
267	- **loguru in a library hijacks the importing program's logging.** Library
268	  modules use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`; only entry points call
269	  `_log.configure()`. Symptom: "my app's log format changed after I added a
270	  dependency."
271	- **`logger.add()` without `logger.remove()` prints everything twice.** loguru
272	  installs a default stderr sink at import. This is the most common loguru bug.
273	- **`diagnose=True` puts local variables in tracebacks** — a credential leak in
274	  production logs. Keep it off outside development.
275	- **`.python-version` is read by pyenv as well as uv.** A stale value silently
276	  changes which interpreter builds the venv. Write it with `uv python pin`.
277	  Use it for your preferred local interpreter (to reuse your local `uv` wheel
278	  cache); keep `requires-python` lower for consumer compatibility, and test both
279	  ends in CI. If either is on EOL Python (`<=3.10`), upgrade with `uv python pin
280	  3.13`, set `requires-python = ">=3.11"` + `ruff.target-version = "py311"`, and
281	  run `uv run ruff check --select UP --fix`.
282	- **`ruff`'s `target-version` should be your `requires-python` floor**, not
283	  your dev pin, or `UP` rewrites code to syntax your declared floor cannot run.
284	- **direnv cannot change `PS1`.** There is no `(.venv)` prompt even when the
285	  env is active — check `which python`, not the prompt. And `.envrc` needs
286	  `direnv allow` after every edit.
287	- **Tyro already has shell completion.** Do not add shtab, argcomplete, or a
288	  `completion` subcommand: `my-tool --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`.
289	  `--tyro-print-completion` is deprecated (a stray `print()` corrupts it), the
290	  bash completion filename must equal the command name, and no package manager
291	  installs completions for you.
292	- **No `[project.scripts]` means `uv tool install` gives the user no command.**
293	  `python -m pkg` is not a substitute for something on `PATH`.
294	- **marimo notebooks are real `.py` files**, so ruff lints them: without
295	  `per-file-ignores` for `notebooks/*` (`E402`, `F401`, `B018`) the gate fails
296	  and the formatter can reorder cell contents.
297	- **A PEP 723 script runs in its own environment.** A helper in `scripts/`
298	  with an inline header cannot `import your_package` unless the package is in
299	  its own `dependencies`.
300	- **`uv sync` does not rebuild a Rust extension after you edit `rust/`.** It
301	  sees the package as installed, does nothing, and you keep running the stale
302	  binary — including the print statements you just added to debug it. Use
303	  `uv sync --reinstall-package <slug>` or `maturin develop --uv`. A compiled
304	  module also needs a hand-written `.pyi`, or type checkers report
305	  `has no member`.
306	- **Never replace the `AGENTS.md`↔`CLAUDE.md` symlink with a real file.** Git
307	  stores it as mode `120000`; two real files drift and only one is right. A
308	  Windows checkout without symlink support materializes a text file containing
309	  the path — that is the corruption, not the fix.
310	- **Do not `uv add -r requirements.txt` when migrating.** A pip freeze is a
311	  flattened graph; that command promotes every transitive pin to a direct
312	  dependency. Add the packages you actually import and let the resolver work.
313	- **uv does not supply non-Python system libraries.** Some scientific stacks
314	  still need conda or OS packages. Say which ones in the README instead of
315	  pretending the migration is complete.
316	- **A tracked `.env` is an incident, not a cleanup.** Rotate every credential
317	  first; history rewriting is a later, separately-approved step. Hand off to
318	  `agent-history-hygiene`.

5	
6	# git-workflow
7	
8	One consistent, opinionated git workflow that scales from a solo weekend
9	project to a multi-person, multi-month repo — so you (and your agents) stop
10	improvising commit messages, branch names, and release habits per project.
11	The defaults here favor a **clean, linear, reviewable history**.
12	
13	Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:
14	
15	| Surface | Question it answers |
16	|---|---|
17	| `references/project-tiers.md` | "Do I commit to `main`, use a `dev` branch, or open PRs?" |
18	| `references/conventional-commits.md` | "What exactly goes in the commit message, including AI provenance?" |
19	| `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` | "How do I run parallel agents without collisions?" |
20	| `references/versioning-and-releases.md` | "When and how do I tag a version?" |
21	| `references/branch-hygiene.md` | "Which local branches are done vs still in-dev?" |
22	| `scripts/branch-status.sh` | Same, as data — classify every local branch. |
23	| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | "Is this commit message valid?" |
24	| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | "How do I do this in lazygit?" (learning aid) |
25	
26	## Core principles
27	
28	1. **Commit messages are English and follow Conventional Commits**, even when
29	   the prompt/conversation is in Chinese. Code history is read by tooling
30	   (changelogs, SemVer bumps) and future collaborators; a mixed-language log
31	   is harder to grep and automate. Prompts stay whatever language you like.
32	2. **Prefer a linear history.** Default to `pull --rebase` and fast-forward
33	   merges; reserve merge commits and squashes for PR integration points. A
34	   linear log makes `git bisect`, `git revert`, and blame legible.
35	3. **One logical change = one commit; one workflow phase = one commit.** For
36	   multi-phase / `/workflows` work, commit at each phase boundary so you can
37	   roll back or resume cleanly if interrupted. Don't batch unrelated changes.
38	4. **Never leak secrets into history.** Secret scanning + agent-transcript
39	   handling is owned by the [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md)
40	   skill — this skill *defers* to it at commit/merge time rather than
41	   reimplementing it.
42	5. **Keep authorship, AI provenance, and cryptographic signing separate.** The
43	   human remains Git author/committer; agent harness + model live in canonical
44	   trailers; SSH/GPG signing proves key possession, not who wrote each line.
45	
46	## Pick your tier first
47	
48	Match the workflow to the project's real collaboration needs, not its
49	ambitions. Promote a tier only when the **signal** actually appears.
50	
51	| Tier | Shape | Branching | Integration | Promote when… |
52	|---|---|---|---|---|
53	| **1 — Solo / early** | one `main` | commit to `main`; short-lived local branches optional | `pull --rebase`, `merge --ff-only` | you need a stable line separate from WIP |
54	| **2 — prod/dev split** | `main` = released, `dev` = integration | feature branches off `dev` | merge to `dev`; fast-forward `dev`→`main` at release | others rely on a deployed/tagged version |
55	| **3 — Team / grown vibe-coding** | `main` always deployable | short-lived `feat/…` etc. → PR | PR review/CI → squash-merge | ≥2 contributors, or you want a per-feature ship+review gate |
56	
57	A **solo vibe-coding** project can jump straight to Tier 3 even with one human:
58	the PR becomes the "ship a feature" boundary that separates finished work from
59	in-progress work, and gives CI a place to run. See
60	`references/project-tiers.md` for per-tier command recipes and the GitHub-Flow
61	summary. Read it when deciding whether to branch/PR or when a project outgrows
62	committing straight to `main`.
63	
64	## Commit messages
65	
66	Format (full spec + type table in `references/conventional-commits.md` — read
67	it when writing a non-obvious commit or wiring `check-commit-msg.sh`):
68	
69	```
70	<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>
71	
72	<body — the "why" for non-trivial agent commits, wrapped ~72 cols>
73	
74	<optional standard/native footers>
75	<canonical agent trailers — AI-Assisted-By / Agent-Transcript / Agent-Plan>
76	```
77	
78	- **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`,
79	  `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`.
80	- **Subject**: imperative mood, lowercase start, no trailing period, keep the
81	  header ≤ ~72 chars. "add retry to client", not "Added retry." / "Adds…".
82	- **Breaking change**: `feat!:` / `refactor(api)!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
83	  footer → drives a **major** SemVer bump.
84	- Validate before committing when unsure:
85	
86	```bash
87	printf 'feat(auth): add token refresh\n' | \
88	  bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh
89	```
90	
91	- Install the message template so the shape is always in front of you:
92	
93	```bash
94	git config commit.template skills/local/git-workflow/assets/commit-template.txt
95	```
96	
97	### Agentic commit contract
98	
99	Use this portable minimum for commits produced with Claude Code, Codex,
100	Cursor, OpenCode, or another coding-agent harness:
101	
102	```text
103	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
104	
105	Explain why the change was needed, the resulting behavior, and meaningful
106	validation. Keep this in English even when the prompt was not English.
107	
108	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
109	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
110	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
111	```
112	
113	- A non-trivial agent commit requires a body. Use the validator's
114	  `--allow-no-body` only for a genuinely self-explanatory change such as a typo.
115	- Repeat `AI-Assisted-By` for every distinct harness/model that materially
116	  contributed. Never invent a vendor email merely to make GitHub show an AI as
117	  a co-author.
118	- Repeat transcript/plan trailers for every staged artifact, using repo-relative
119	  paths. Omit `Agent-Plan` when no plan file is in the commit.
120	- Preserve tool-native metadata (for example Claude's `Co-Authored-By`) as
121	  additive evidence. Put the canonical fields in the **final Git trailer
122	  block** so `git interpret-trailers --parse` can query them.
123	- When `agent-history-hygiene` is installed, generate the block from the staged
124	  snapshot instead of copying paths/model names by hand:
125	
126	```bash
127	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
128	```
129	
130	Validate the complete message before committing:
131	
132	```bash
133	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
134	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
135	```
136	
137	Cryptographic signing is opt-in and user-owned. Configure SSH/GPG signing only
138	when the user explicitly asks; never silently change global Git or harness
139	settings. A vendor-signed cloud-agent commit must not be amended solely to add
140	metadata, because amending replaces the signed commit object.
141	
142	## Branch naming
143	
144	Use a `<prefix>/<kebab-desc>` namespace so branches sort and clean up by
145	intent, and so agent-generated branches are visually distinct from yours:
146	
147	- **Human intent**: `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `refactor/…`,
148	  `exp/…` (throwaway experiments). Optionally embed an issue: `feat/123-oauth`.
149	- **Agent / vibe-coding**: `agent/<desc>` — a dedicated namespace you can bulk-
150	  triage or delete separately from hand-authored branches.
151	- **Claude worktrees**: `worktree-<name>` (auto-created by `claude --worktree`)
152	  is a third namespace — see below.
153	
154	Keeping these separate is what makes `branch-status.sh` and
155	`git branch --list 'agent/*'` cleanup targeted rather than risky.
156	
157	## Merge & sync
158	
159	Set linear-history defaults (per-repo, or `--global` to your taste):
160	
161	```bash
162	git config pull.rebase true      # rebase local work onto upstream on pull
163	git config merge.ff only         # refuse merges that can't fast-forward
164	```
165	
166	- **Solo/local**: `git pull --rebase`, then `git merge --ff-only <branch>` to
167	  land a short-lived branch with no merge commit.
168	- **PRs (Tier 3)**: prefer **squash-merge** for vibe-coding branches (collapses
169	  noisy WIP into one clean `feat: …` commit on `main`); use **rebase-merge**
170	  when every commit is already meaningful and you want them preserved.
171	- Drive PRs from the terminal with the **forge CLI** — `gh` (GitHub) or `glab`
172	  (GitLab). These are strongly recommended (not required — the scripts here
173	  degrade to plain git if absent):
174	
175	```bash
176	gh pr create --fill            # or: glab mr create --fill
177	gh pr checks                   # watch CI
178	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch   # glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch
179	```
180	
181	  The vendored `create-pull-request` skill (github-workflow group) is a
182	  companion for richer PR bodies.
183	
184	## Worktrees for parallel agents
185	
186	Run each parallel agent/session in its own git worktree so file edits never
187	collide. Full mechanics + caveats in `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md`
188	— read it before setting up parallel agents or debugging a missing `.env` in
189	a worktree.
190	
191	Essentials:
192	
193	```bash
194	claude --worktree feature-auth   # → .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/
195	```
196	
197	- Worktrees branch from `origin/HEAD` by default; set `worktree.baseRef: "head"`
198	  in settings to branch from your local HEAD (unpushed work).
199	- Subagents: add `isolation: worktree` frontmatter, or ask Claude to "use
200	  worktrees for your agents".
201	- **Gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`** so worktree contents don't show as
202	  untracked files in the main checkout.
203	- Bring **gitignored** files (e.g. `.env`) into new worktrees with a
204	  `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root (see `assets/worktreeinclude.template`).
205	  It uses `.gitignore` syntax and copies **only gitignored** matches — already-
206	  tracked files are in the checkout already, so don't list them.
207	- Bonus: because SpecStory tracks transcripts by *directory*, a worktree's
208	  fresh dir cleanly separates each parallel agent's chat history.
209	
210	## Versioning & releases
211	
212	Use **SemVer** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) and let commit types imply the bump:
213	`fix:` → PATCH, `feat:` → MINOR, `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → MAJOR. Tag releases
214	with an **annotated, `v`-prefixed** tag on the release commit:
215	
216	```bash
217	git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "release: v1.4.0" && git push origin v1.4.0
218	```
219	
220	When the whole project **is** a Python package, make the git tag the single
221	source of truth (setuptools-scm or hatch-vcs) instead of hand-editing a
222	version string. Details + config in `references/versioning-and-releases.md` —
223	read it when cutting a release or wiring package versioning.
224	
225	## Before you merge / ship
226	
227	1. **Phase commits**: ensure each phase of the work is its own commit (easy
228	   rollback / resume).
229	2. **Dev-env reproducibility (optional, recommended)**: commit
230	   `.vscode/settings.json` + `.vscode/extensions.json` so a fresh clone gets
231	   the same editor setup. (These are *tracked*, so they don't belong in
232	   `.worktreeinclude`.)
233	3. **Secret + agent-artifact hygiene** — defer to
234	   [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md):
235	
236	```bash
237	# clean = exit 0; redacted = 10; leaks = 20 → stop and remediate
238	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
239	```
240	
241	   If the project **doesn't** check in agent transcripts/plans, drop them
242	   before a squash-merge; if it does, stage them with that skill's
243	   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`. Either way, a leaked secret is remediated via
244	   its `references/remediation.md` (rotate first — never reflexive
245	   `git push --force`).
246	4. **Agentic squash metadata**: a squash merge creates a new commit, so copy the
247	   canonical `AI-Assisted-By` / artifact trailers into the squash message. The
248	   source commit's cryptographic signature cannot survive object replacement.
249	5. **Branch cleanup** after the PR merges:
250	
251	```bash
252	git fetch --prune
253	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/branch-status.sh   # find gone/merged/stale
254	```
255	
256	## When to use this skill
257	
258	- "Commit this" / "幫我 commit" / "整理一下 git" / "write a commit message".
259	- "Should I branch or just commit to main?" / "should I open a PR?".
260	- "Set up worktrees for parallel agents" / "carry my `.env` into the worktree".
261	- "How do I tag / release a version?" / "bump the version".

276	
277	- **`scripts/branch-status.sh [--json] [--stale-days N] [--help]`** — classify
278	  every local branch as `active` / `merged` / `gone` (upstream deleted, e.g.
279	  after a squash-merge) / `stale` (no commits in N days, default 30). TSV on
280	  stdout by default, `--json` for callers, prose on stderr. Always exits 0
281	  (state is data). Enriches `merged`/`gone` with `gh`/`glab` when available,
282	  falling back to pure git otherwise.
283	- **`scripts/check-commit-msg.sh [--file PATH] [--agentic] [--staged] [--allow-no-body] [--types]`**
284	  — default mode validates a Conventional Commits header. `--agentic` also
285	  requires an English body + canonical harness/model trailers; `--staged`
286	  cross-checks transcript/plan paths against the index. Exit **0** valid /
287	  **1** invalid / **2** bad args or repository context.
288	
289	## Bundled assets
290	
291	- `assets/commit-template.txt` — commit message skeleton for
292	  `git config commit.template`.
293	- `assets/worktreeinclude.template` — example `.worktreeinclude` (gitignored
294	  env files only; annotated so tracked files aren't added by mistake).
295	
296	## Reference files
297	
298	- `references/project-tiers.md` — read when deciding main-vs-dev-vs-PR or when
299	  a project outgrows its current tier. Per-tier recipes + GitHub-Flow summary.
300	- `references/conventional-commits.md` — read when writing a non-trivial commit
301	  or wiring the validator. Full type table, footers, examples.
302	- `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` — read before setting up parallel
303	  agents or debugging worktree file-copy / cleanup issues.
304	- `references/versioning-and-releases.md` — read when cutting a release or
305	  wiring Python tag-driven versioning (setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs).
306	- `references/branch-hygiene.md` — read when local branches are confusing
307	  (PR merged but branch lingers; work continued after merge).
308	- `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` — read when you'd rather drive git through
309	  lazygit; a learning aid, safe to ignore once the CLI is second nature.
310	
311	## Gotchas
312	
313	- **`merge.ff only` refuses a diverged pull.** If upstream moved and you have
314	  local commits, a plain `git pull`/`merge` errors instead of making a merge
315	  commit — that's intended. Resolve with `git pull --rebase` (or an explicit
316	  `git merge --no-ff` when you truly want the merge commit).
317	- **Squash-merge orphans the source branch.** After a squashed PR, the branch's
318	  commits never appear on `main`, so `git branch --merged` won't list it; it
319	  shows up as `gone` upstream (`git branch -vv`). `branch-status.sh` classifies
320	  this correctly — delete with `git branch -D`, not `-d`.
321	- **A PR can merge and work still continue on the branch.** "Merged" is not
322	  always "done". `branch-status.sh` flags `gone` upstream but won't delete —
323	  confirm the branch has no un-pushed commits before removing it.
324	- **Tracked files in `.worktreeinclude` do nothing.** It copies only gitignored
325	  matches. A committed `.vscode/settings.json` is already in the worktree; put
326	  only truly-ignored files (`.env`, `.env.local`, `config/secrets.json`) there.
327	- **`.worktreeinclude` is skipped with a custom `WorktreeCreate` hook.** For
328	  non-git VCS (SVN/Perforce/hg) the hook replaces default logic — copy local
329	  files inside the hook script instead.
330	- **English-commit rule holds under Chinese prompts.** Don't mirror the
331	  prompt's language into the commit subject; translate the intent to English.
332	- **A commit template does not affect `git commit -m`.** Agent harnesses usually
333	  [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] `-m` directly, so the template is guidance, not enforcement. Use
334	  `check-commit-msg.sh --agentic` for the actual contract.
335	- **Native attribution is not cryptographic signing.** `Co-Authored-By` and
336	  `AI-Assisted-By` are message metadata; a Verified badge comes from a signed
337	  commit object. Preserve both when present, but do not describe them as the
338	  same guarantee.
339	- **Don't tag before the release commit exists.** An annotated tag points at a
340	  commit — create/land the release commit first, then `git tag -a`, then push
341	  the tag. A tag on the wrong commit means re-tagging (`-f`) and a force-push.
342	- **`gh`/`glab` are optional.** Recommend them, but never make a workflow step
343	  hard-depend on a forge CLI being installed or authenticated.
344
````

11	# Compatibility: macOS system Bash 3.2+.

13	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

15	# shellcheck source=forge.sh
16	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/forge.sh"
17	
18	# Configurable worktree root (relative to repo root).
19	FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT="${FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT:-.worktrees}"
20	
21	usage() {
22	  cat <<'EOF'
23	Usage: forge-worktree.sh <subcommand> [args]
24	
25	Subcommands:
26	  start <issue-number>    Create a branch + worktree for the issue.
27	                          Branch: issue/<number>-<slug>
28	                          Worktree: .worktrees/issue-<number>/
29	  finish <issue-number>   Push the branch and create a PR linking to the issue.

34	  --base BRANCH           Base branch to create from (default: auto-detected).
35	  --draft                 Create PR as draft (finish only).
36	  -h, --help              Show this help and exit.
37	
38	Environment:
39	  FORGE_WORKTREE_ROOT     Worktree directory (default: .worktrees).
40	EOF
41	}
42	
43	subcmd=""
44	issue_num=""
45	agent_prefix=0
46	base_branch=""
47	draft=0
48

54	    --base) base_branch="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	    --draft) draft=1; shift ;;

59	      ;;
60	    *)

64	  esac

67	# Remaining args after subcommand

69	  case "$1" in
70	    --agent) agent_prefix=1; shift ;;
71	    --base) base_branch="$2"; shift 2 ;;
72	    --draft) draft=1; shift ;;

75	      ;;
76	    *)

78	      ;;
79	  esac
80	done
81	
82	[ -z "$subcmd" ] && { usage; exit 1; }
83	
84	# Ensure we're in a git repo and detect the forge

86	_forge_require_cli
87	
88	# Resolve repo root

96	# start
97	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	
99	cmd_start() {
100	  [ -z "$issue_num" ] && _forge_die "start requires an issue number" 1
101	
102	  _forge_log "Fetching issue #$issue_num..."
103	  local issue_json
104	  issue_json="$(forge_issue_view "$issue_num" --json)"
105	
106	  # Extract title for slug
107	  local issue_title
108	  case "$FORGE_TYPE" in
109	    github)
110	      issue_title="$(printf '%s' "$issue_json" | sed -n 's/.*"title":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)"
111	      ;;
112	    gitlab)
113	      issue_title="$(printf '%s' "$issue_json" | sed -n 's/.*"title":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)"
114	      ;;
115	  esac

117	  if [ -z "$issue_title" ]; then
118	    _forge_warn "could not extract issue title; using issue number only"
119	    issue_title="issue-$issue_num"
120	  fi
121	
122	  local slug
123	  slug="$(forge_slugify "$issue_title")"
124	
125	  local branch_name
126	  if [ "$agent_prefix" -eq 1 ]; then

129	    branch_name="issue/${issue_num}-${slug}"

131	
132	  local worktree_path="$worktree_root/issue-${issue_num}"
133

146	      _forge_log "Creating worktree for existing branch..."

149	  else

164	  forge_issue_label "$issue_num" --add "in-progress" 2>/dev/null || true

168	  _forge_log "Issue:    #$issue_num — $issue_title"
169	  _forge_log "Branch:   $branch_name"
170	  _forge_log "Worktree: $worktree_path"
171	  _forge_log ""
172	  _forge_log "To start working:"
173	  _forge_log "  cd $worktree_path"
174	}
175	
176	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
177	# finish
178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

183	  # Find the branch for this issue

````text
1	# Versioning & releases
2	
3	Read this when cutting a release, tagging a version, or wiring a Python package
4	so its version comes from the git tag. Covers [SemVer](https://semver.org/),
5	annotated tags, and tag-driven Python versioning.
6	
7	## Table of contents
8	
9	1. [SemVer in one paragraph](#semver-in-one-paragraph)
10	2. [Mapping commits to bumps](#mapping-commits-to-bumps)
11	3. [Tagging a release](#tagging-a-release)
12	4. [When to tag](#when-to-tag)
13	5. [Python: git tag as single source of truth](#python-git-tag-as-single-source-of-truth)
14	6. [Changelog](#changelog)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## SemVer in one paragraph
19	
20	`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Bump **MAJOR** for incompatible API changes, **MINOR** for
21	backward-compatible features, **PATCH** for backward-compatible fixes.
22	Pre-release and build metadata append as `-rc.1` / `+build.5`
23	(e.g. `2.0.0-rc.1`). Below `1.0.0` anything may change; `1.0.0` is the
24	commitment to a stable public API.
25	
26	## Mapping commits to bumps
27	
28	If commits follow [Conventional Commits](conventional-commits.md), the bump is
29	mechanical:
30	
31	- `fix:` / `perf:` → PATCH
32	- `feat:` → MINOR
33	- `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` → MAJOR
34	
35	Tools like [`commitizen`](https://commitizen-tools.github.io/commitizen/) or
36	`semantic-release` can compute the next version and changelog from the log.
37	
38	## Tagging a release
39	
40	Use an **annotated**, `v`-prefixed tag on the release commit:
41	
42	```bash
43	git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "release: v1.4.0"
44	git push origin v1.4.0
45	# or push commits + their tags together:
46	git commit ... && git push --follow-tags
47	```
48	
49	- **Annotated** (`-a`) tags store tagger, date, and message and are the right
50	  choice for releases (lightweight tags are just a moving label).
51	- Create the tag **on the commit that is the release** — don't tag ahead of it.
52	  Fixing a mis-placed tag means `git tag -f` + a force-push of the tag, which
53	  is disruptive if others already fetched it.
54	- List/inspect: `git tag --list 'v1.*'`, `git show v1.4.0`.
55	
56	## When to tag
57	
58	- **Applications/services**: at each deploy boundary worth returning to, or per
59	  release train (`v2025.07.0`-style calendar versions are also fine if that's
60	  your convention).
61	- **Libraries/packages**: at every published version — the tag *is* the release
62	  users depend on.
63	- Tag from `main` (Tier 3) or the promoted release commit (Tier 2). Don't tag
64	  arbitrary WIP commits.
65	
66	## Python: git tag as single source of truth
67	
68	When the whole repo **is** a Python package, don't hand-maintain a version
69	string in `__init__.py` *and* `pyproject.toml` *and* a git tag — derive it from
70	the tag. See the [Python Packaging guide on single-sourcing the version](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/).
71	
72	**setuptools backend** — [setuptools-scm](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/):
73	
74	```toml
75	[build-system]
76	requires = ["setuptools>=64", "setuptools-scm>=8"]
77	build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
78	
79	[project]
80	name = "yourpkg"
81	dynamic = ["version"]
82	
83	[tool.setuptools_scm]
84	# version comes from the latest git tag; a dev suffix is added between tags
85	```
86	
87	**Hatch backend** — [hatch-vcs](https://pypi.org/project/hatch-vcs/):
88	
89	```toml
90	[build-system]
91	requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
92	build-backend = "hatchling.build"
93	
94	[project]
95	name = "yourpkg"
96	dynamic = ["version"]
97	
98	[tool.hatch.version]
99	source = "vcs"
100	```
101	
102	Notes:
103	- Tags must be **PEP 440-compatible** once parsed. `vX.Y.Z` works (the `v` is
104	  stripped); avoid tags that don't map to PEP 440.
105	- Version is resolved at **build/install time**. Editable/dev installs can show
106	  a stale value until rebuilt — expected behavior, not a bug.
107	- In CI, cut the release by pushing the tag; the build then stamps the matching
108	  version. Verify the tag produces the expected version in CI before publishing.
109	
110	## Changelog
111	
112	Keep a human-readable `CHANGELOG.md` (the
113	[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) format is a good default), or
114	generate it from Conventional Commits with `commitizen`/`semantic-release`.
115	Either way, the changelog entry and the tag should agree on the version.
116
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Worktrees for parallel agents
2	
3	Read this before setting up parallel Claude Code sessions/agents, or when
4	debugging a worktree that's missing a gitignored file (like `.env`) or won't
5	clean up. Based on the official
6	[Claude Code worktrees docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees) and
7	[`git worktree`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree).
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [Why worktrees](#why-worktrees)
12	2. [Starting a worktree](#starting-a-worktree)
13	3. [Choosing the base branch](#choosing-the-base-branch)
14	4. [Copying gitignored files (`.worktreeinclude`)](#copying-gitignored-files-worktreeinclude)
15	5. [Isolating subagents](#isolating-subagents)
16	6. [SpecStory separation bonus](#specstory-separation-bonus)
17	7. [Cleanup](#cleanup)
18	8. [Manual worktrees & non-git VCS](#manual-worktrees--non-git-vcs)
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Why worktrees
23	
24	A git worktree is a separate working directory with its own files and branch,
25	sharing the same repo history and remote. Running each parallel agent/session
26	in its own worktree means edits in one never touch another — one terminal
27	builds a feature while a second fixes a bug, with zero file collisions.
28	
29	## Starting a worktree
30	
31	```bash
32	claude --worktree feature-auth   # or -w
33	# → creates .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/ on branch worktree-feature-auth
34	claude --worktree                # omit the name → generates e.g. bright-running-fox
35	```
36	
37	You can also ask Claude to "work in a worktree" mid-session (it uses the
38	`EnterWorktree` tool). **Add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`** so worktree
39	contents don't appear as untracked files in your main checkout.
40	
41	## Choosing the base branch
42	
43	- Default: worktrees branch from `origin/HEAD` (your default branch), so they
44	  start from a clean tree matching the remote.
45	- To branch from your **local HEAD** (carrying unpushed commits / feature-branch
46	  state — useful for isolating subagents on in-progress work), set in settings:
47	
48	```json
49	{ "worktree": { "baseRef": "head" } }
50	```
51	
52	  Only `"fresh"` (default) or `"head"` are accepted — not arbitrary refs.
53	- Branch from a specific PR: `claude --worktree "#1234"` →
54	  `.claude/worktrees/pr-1234`.
55	
56	## Copying gitignored files (`.worktreeinclude`)
57	
58	A worktree is a fresh checkout, so untracked files like `.env` are **not**
59	present. Add a `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root to copy them in
60	automatically. It uses `.gitignore` syntax and copies **only files that match a
61	pattern *and* are gitignored** — tracked files are never duplicated.
62	
63	```text
64	# .worktreeinclude — gitignored files to carry into new worktrees
65	.env
66	.env.local
67	config/secrets.json
68	```
69	
70	**Key correction to a common misconception:** a committed
71	`.vscode/settings.json` is *tracked*, so it's already in the worktree checkout
72	— listing it here does nothing. Only put genuinely-ignored files here. Applies
73	to `--worktree`, subagent worktrees, and desktop parallel sessions.
74	
75	## Isolating subagents
76	
77	Give parallel subagents their own worktrees so their edits don't conflict:
78	
79	- Ask Claude to "use worktrees for your agents", or
80	- set it permanently on a custom subagent with frontmatter:
81	
82	```yaml
83	---
84	name: my-agent
85	isolation: worktree
86	---
87	```
88	
89	Each subagent gets a temporary worktree, removed automatically when it finishes
90	without changes. Subagent worktrees use the same base branch as `--worktree`.
91	
92	## SpecStory separation bonus
93	
94	SpecStory tracks transcripts by **directory**, not branch. Because each
95	worktree is a fresh directory, parallel agents each accumulate their chat
96	history under their own `.specstory/` — a clean cut that avoids interleaving
97	transcripts from concurrent sessions.
98	
99	## Cleanup
100	
101	On exiting a worktree session:
102	
103	- **No changes/commits**: worktree + branch removed automatically (named
104	  sessions prompt so you can keep them).
105	- **Uncommitted changes / untracked / new commits**: Claude prompts to keep or
106	  remove.
107	- **Non-interactive `-p` runs**: not cleaned up automatically — remove with
108	  `git worktree remove` (add `--force` if it has uncommitted work).
109	
110	Subagent/background worktrees are swept once older than `cleanupPeriodDays`,
111	provided they have no uncommitted changes/untracked files/unpushed commits.
112	
113	## Manual worktrees & non-git VCS
114	
115	Full manual control:
116	
117	```bash
118	git worktree add ../proj-feature-a -b feature-a   # new branch
119	git worktree add ../proj-bugfix bugfix-123        # existing branch
120	git worktree list
121	git worktree remove ../proj-feature-a
122	```
123	
124	Remember to reinitialize the dev environment in each new worktree (install
125	deps, create venvs). For **non-git VCS** (SVN/Perforce/hg), configure
126	`WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks — note that `.worktreeinclude` is **not
127	processed** when a custom hook replaces the default git logic, so copy local
128	config files inside the hook script instead.
129	
130	## Worktrees in a submodule superproject
131	
132	A worktree of a **superproject** starts with every submodule uninitialized, so
133	it is the wrong tool for work inside a child repo. Create a worktree of the
134	**child** instead, under `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`. The
135	`superproject-workspace` skill's
136	`superproject.py worktree add <child> <branch>` does this, including the
137	`.gitignore` entry and branching pins from their recorded gitlink. See its
138	`references/worktrees.md`.
139
````

````text
1	# uv and pyproject.toml
2	
3	Load this when writing or repairing `pyproject.toml`, deciding what goes in a
4	lockfile, choosing a build backend, pinning the interpreter, or publishing.
5	
6	uv's CLI surface changes between minor versions. When you are unsure of a flag,
7	fetch <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/> rather than guessing.
8	
9	## The commands that matter
10	
11	| Goal | Command |
12	|---|---|
13	| Start a project | `uv init --package --lib` (or `--app`) |
14	| Add a runtime dependency | `uv add httpx` |
15	| Add dev tooling | `uv add --dev pytest ruff` |
16	| Add to a named group | `uv add --group docs mkdocs-material` |
17	| Add a published extra | `uv add --optional postgres asyncpg` |
18	| Recreate the env from the lock | `uv sync` |
19	| Fail instead of re-resolving | `uv sync --locked` (use this in CI) |
20	| Check the lock is current | `uv lock --check` |
21	| Pin the interpreter | `uv python pin 3.13` |
22	| Run anything | `uv run <cmd>` |
23	| Bump the version | `uv version --bump minor` |
24	| Build + publish | `uv build && uv publish` |
25	
26	`uv run` re-syncs before running. In a hot loop where you know the environment
27	is current, `uv run --no-sync` skips it.
28	
29	## Groups vs extras
30	
31	This is the distinction people get wrong, and getting it wrong ships your test
32	runner to your users.
33	
34	```toml
35	[project.optional-dependencies]   # PUBLISHED. `pip install yourpkg[postgres]`
36	postgres = ["asyncpg>=0.30"]
37	
38	[dependency-groups]               # LOCAL ONLY. PEP 735. Never published.
39	dev = ["pytest>=8.3", "ruff>=0.9"]
40	docs = ["mkdocs-material>=9.5"]
41	```
42	
43	`dev` is special-cased: `uv sync` and `uv run` include it by default. Other
44	groups need `--group docs`. `--no-default-groups` gives a runtime-only env.
45	
46	A dev tool in `optional-dependencies` is a real defect: it appears in your
47	package metadata, resolves into your users' dependency graph if they ever
48	install the extra, and cannot be removed without a release.
49	
50	> Interop note: some tooling still generates a `docs` **extra** — for example
51	> the `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill writes `[project.optional-dependencies]
52	> docs`. That keeps working (`uv sync --extra docs`); it is not worth a
53	> migration unless you are publishing the package.
54	
55	## Lockfile policy
56	
57	Commit `uv.lock`. For applications and CLIs this is obvious. For libraries it
58	is also right, and the usual objection is based on a misunderstanding:
59	
60	**`uv.lock` never constrains your users.** When someone installs your package
61	as a dependency, their resolver reads `[project.dependencies]` and ignores your
62	lock entirely. The lock pins *your* development and CI environment, which is
63	exactly what you want reproducible.
64	
65	What the lock does not do is prove your declared ranges are honest. If you
66	publish a library and want to verify that your declared `requires-python` and
67	`[project.dependencies]` floors actually [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] tests, run an on-demand isolated
68	check (using `--isolated` so it never downgrades your working `.venv`):
69	
70	```bash
71	uv run --isolated --python 3.11 --resolution lowest-direct pytest
72	```
73	
74	## Interpreter pinning vs `requires-python` compatibility
75	
76	`.python-version` and `requires-python` solve opposite problems. Conflating
77	them (which `uv init` does by default) either slows down local setup or locks
78	out downstream users:
79	
80	| Setting | Purpose | How to choose |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `.python-version` (`--python-pin`) | Local dev `.venv` interpreter | Match the user's preferred local Python (or let `--python-pin auto` pick an already-installed `3.11+` interpreter) so `uv sync` skips downloading Python and reuses the local `uv` wheel cache. |
83	| `requires-python` (`--python-floor`) | Downstream package compatibility floor | Set to the **oldest non-EOL Python (`>=3.11`)** unless you genuinely use newer language/stdlib features or must target a legacy host. |
84	
85	Put both ends in the CI matrix (`[python_floor, python_pin]`). `.python-version`
86	is also read by pyenv; on a machine with both, a stale value changes which
87	interpreter builds the venv with no warning.
88	
89	### Choosing `requires-python` by actual features used
90	
91	Per <https://devguide.python.org/versions/>, Python **3.10 reached End-of-Life
92	in October 2026**. Default to `>=3.11` and only raise the floor when runtime
93	code actually needs a newer feature (remember: `from __future__ import
94	annotations` makes newer type-annotation syntax work on older runtimes without
95	raising `requires-python`):
96	
97	| Floor | Raise to this only when runtime code uses |
98	|---|---|
99	| `>=3.10` (EOL) | Legacy deployment target only (e.g. unupgraded Ubuntu 22.04 host). Supports runtime `X \| Y` unions (PEP 604) and `match`/`case`. |
100	| `>=3.11` **(default)** | Oldest non-EOL Python. Stdlib `tomllib`, `enum.StrEnum`, `typing.Self`, `ExceptionGroup` / `except*`, `asyncio.TaskGroup`. |
101	| `>=3.12` | `type X = ...` statements and PEP 695 generic syntax (`def f[T]()`), `@typing.override`, `itertools.batched`, `Path.walk`. |
102	| `>=3.13` | PEP 696 `TypeVar` defaults (`T = int`), `warnings.deprecated`, free-threaded / JIT experimentation. |
103	
104	### Upgrading a project off an EOL Python (`<=3.10`)
105	
106	When a user's local environment or repository is still on Python `<=3.10`,
107	recommend and execute these four steps together:
108	
109	```bash
110	# 1. Install and pin a modern dev interpreter (3.13 or user's preferred 3.11+)
111	uv python install 3.13 && uv python pin 3.13
112	
113	# 2. In pyproject.toml, set:
114	#    requires-python = ">=3.11"
115	#    [tool.ruff] target-version = "py311"
116	
117	# 3. Let ruff's pyupgrade (UP) rules modernize legacy syntax/typing automatically
118	uv run ruff check --select UP --fix
119	
120	# 4. Re-lock and run the full gate
121	uv lock && uv sync && just check
122	```
123	
124	## Dependency bounds for installable packages
125	
126	When someone installs your package (`pip install`, `uv add`, `uv tool install`),
127	their resolver intersects your `[project.dependencies]` with everything else in
128	their environment. Two habits keep your package easy to install:
129	
130	1. **Relax `uv add`'s lower bound.** `uv add foo` writes
131	   `foo>=<version-released-today>` (e.g. `pydantic-settings>=2.10.1`). If your
132	   package only uses APIs present since `2.0`, relax the entry in
133	   `[project.dependencies]` to `"pydantic-settings>=2.0"`. `uv.lock` still keeps
134	   your dev and CI environment on `2.10.1`.
135	2. **Do not add upper caps (`<`, `~=`, `==`) in `[project.dependencies]`.**
136	   Upper-capping `"pydantic>=2.0,<2.11"` or `"tyro~=0.9"` forces solver deadlocks
137	   for consumers the day a compatible minor version ships. Only add an upper
138	   exclusion (`!=x.y.z` or `<major`) after a specific release is proven broken
139	   with your code.
140	
141	## Build backends
142	
143	| Backend | When |
144	|---|---|
145	| `hatchling` | default. Plugin ecosystem (`hatch-vcs` for git-tag versions) |
146	| `uv_build` | lean, fast, no plugins. Fine for a pure-Python package |
147	| `maturin` | any Rust/PyO3 extension |
148	| `scikit-build-core` | C/C++/CMake extensions |
149	
150	With a src layout and a hyphenated project name, name the package directory
151	explicitly so the backend does not have to guess:
152	
153	```toml
154	[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
155	packages = ["src/my_tool"]
156	```
157	
158	## Distribution
159	
160	Tier 0, and enough for most internal tools — no PyPI account needed:
161	
162	```bash
163	uv tool install git+https://github.com/owner/repo@v0.1.0
164	uvx --from git+https://github.com/owner/repo my-tool --help   # run once
165	```
166	
167	Both require `[project.scripts]`. A package that can only be run as
168	`python -m pkg` gives the installer no command on `PATH`.
169	
170	For PyPI, use Trusted Publishing (OIDC): configure the publisher on PyPI for
171	`owner/repo` + workflow filename, then give the job `id-token: write`. No API
172	token in Actions secrets, nothing to rotate or leak.
173	
174	```yaml
175	permissions:
176	  id-token: write
177	steps:
178	  - run: uv build
179	  - run: uv publish        # picks up the OIDC token automatically
180	```
181	
182	## Workspaces
183	
184	For a monorepo of related packages, one lockfile and one venv for all of them:
185	
186	```toml
187	[tool.uv.workspace]
188	members = ["packages/*"]
189	
190	[tool.uv.sources]
191	my-core = { workspace = true }
192	```
193	
194	Members share the resolution, so a version conflict between two members is a
195	hard error rather than two silently different environments. If the packages
196	genuinely need different dependency versions, they are not a workspace.
197
````

245	def apply_markers(text: str, profile: str) -> str:
246	    """Drop `# __IF:a,b__ ... # __END__` blocks that this profile does not want.
247	
248	    Marker lines are always removed; only the body between them is conditional.
249	    """
250	    out: list[str] = []
251	    keep_stack: list[bool] = []

254	    # between top-level defs is required formatting, not slack.
255	    squeeze = False
256	    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
257	        if match := _IF.match(line):
258	            names = [name.strip() for name in match.group(1).split(",") if name.strip()]
259	            keep_stack.append(profile in names)
260	            continue
261	        if _END.match(line):
262	            if not keep_stack:
263	                die("unbalanced __END__ marker in template", 4)
264	            squeeze = not keep_stack.pop()
265	            continue
266	        if not all(keep_stack):
267	            continue
268	        if squeeze and not line.strip():
269	            if out and not out[-1].strip():
270	                continue
271	        squeeze = False
272	        out.append(line)
273	    if keep_stack:
274	        die("unclosed __IF__ marker in template", 4)
275	    return "".join(out)

382	        ".env is tracked by git" if tracked_env else ".env not tracked",
383	        "git rm --cached .env, add it to .gitignore, ROTATE every credential it held, "
384	        "and only then consider rewriting history" if tracked_env else "")
385	
386	    ignore = (root / ".gitignore").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") \
387	        if (root / ".gitignore").exists() else ""
388	    missing = [entry for entry in (".venv", ".env") if entry not in ignore]
389	    add("gitignore-basics", "warn" if missing else "[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]",
390	        f"not ignored: {', '.join(missing)}" if missing else ".venv and .env ignored",
391	        f"add {' and '.join(missing)} to .gitignore" if missing else "")
392	
393	    return checks
394	
395	
396	def plan(checks: list[Check]) -> list[dict]:
397	    by_id = {check.id: check for check in checks}
398	    steps = []
399	    for title, ids in RUNGS:
400	        outstanding = [i for i in ids if i in by_id and by_id[i].status in {"warn", "fail"}]
401	        if outstanding:
402	            steps.append({"step": len(steps) + 1, "action": title, "resolves": outstanding})
403	    return steps
404	
405	
406	def render_table(checks: list[Check], steps: list[dict]) -> str:
407	    mark = {"[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]": "ok  ", "warn": "WARN", "fail": "FAIL", "n/a": "-   "}
408	    width = max(len(check.id) for check in checks)
409	    lines = [f"{mark[c.status]}  {c.id.ljust(width)}  {c.evidence}" for c in checks]
410	    if steps:
411	        lines.append("")
412	        lines.append("Migration plan (one rung per pull request):")
413	        for step in steps:
414	            lines.append(f"  {step['step']}. {step['action']}")
415	            lines.append(f"     resolves: {', '.join(step['resolves'])}")
416	    return "\n".join(lines)
417	
418	
419	@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
420	class Args:
421	    """Score a Python project against modern-project conventions. Read-only."""
422	
423	    path: tyro.conf.Positional[str] = "."
424	    """Project root to audit."""
425	
426	    format: Literal["json", "table"] = "json"
427	    """json for machines, table for humans."""
428	
429	    fail_on: Literal["fail", "warn", "never"] = "fail"
430	    """Lowest status that makes this exit non-zero."""
431	
432	
433	def main(args: Args) -> None:
434	    root = Path(args.path).expanduser().resolve()
435	    if not root.is_dir():
436	        print(f"error: {root} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
437	        raise SystemExit(3)
438	
439	    checks = audit(root)
440	    steps = plan(checks)
441	    counts = {status: sum(1 for c in checks if c.status == status)
442	              for status in ("[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]", "warn", "fail", "n/a")}
443	
444	    if args.format == "table":
445	        print(render_table(checks, steps))
446	    else:
447	        print(json.dumps({
448	            "path": str(root),
449	            "summary": counts,
450	            "checks": [dataclasses.asdict(check) for check in checks],
451	            "migration_plan": steps,
452	        }, indent=2))
453	
454	    print(
455	        f"{counts['[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]']} [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], {counts['warn']} warn, {counts['fail']} fail "
456	        f"({counts['n/a']} n/a)",
457	        file=sys.stderr,
458	    )
459	    threshold = {"fail": 2, "warn": 1, "never": 99}[args.fail_on]
460	    if any(RANK[check.status] >= threshold for check in checks):
461	        raise SystemExit(4)
462	
463	
464	if __name__ == "__main__":
465	    os.environ.setdefault("COLUMNS", "100")
466	    try:
467	        main(tyro.cli(Args, prog="audit-python-project.py", description=__doc__))
468	    except SystemExit:
469	        raise
470	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - top-level guard, message is the contract
471	        print(f"error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
472	        raise SystemExit(1) from exc
473

1	# PROJECT_SLUG_PLACEHOLDER - agent guide
2	
3	`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file. Edit either path; never replace the
4	symlink with a real file.
5	
6	## Ground rules
7	
8	- **Use `just`.** `just --list` is the complete, supported command surface. If
9	  you need an operation that is not there, add a recipe rather than inventing a
10	  one-off command.
11	- **Never call `pip`.** Dependencies change through `uv add` / `uv remove`,
12	  which update `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` together. A `uv pip install` is
13	  erased by the next `uv sync`.
14	- **`just check` must [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] before you claim a change is done.** It is exactly
15	  what CI runs.
16	- **Dev tooling goes in `[dependency-groups]`, runtime deps in
17	  `[project.dependencies]`.** `uv add --dev <pkg>` for the former.
18	- **Secrets live in `.env`, which is gitignored.** When you add a setting, add
19	  it to `settings.py` *and* to `.env.example` with a placeholder value.
20	
21	## Layout
22	
23	src layout, so `uv run pytest` imports the INSTALLED package rather than the
24	working directory. `notebooks/` and `scripts/` may import the package; the
25	package imports neither.
26	
27	```
28	src/PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/
29	  core.py                         domain logic; stdlib logging only, no side effects
30	# __IF:cli,lib,api,ml,rust__
31	  _log.py                         loguru setup; called by entry points, never at import
32	  settings.py                     pydantic-settings; defaults < .env < environment
33	  cli/                            one frozen dataclass per subcommand
34	# __END__
35	# __IF:api__
36	  api/app.py                      FastAPI app; /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json
37	# __END__
38	tests/                            pytest; mirrors src/ module for module
39	scripts/                          repo helpers, NOT importable from the package
40	# __IF:ml__
41	notebooks/                        marimo notebooks; also runnable as CLIs
42	# __END__
43	# __IF:rust__
44	rust/                             PyO3 crate compiled into PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER._rust
45	# __END__
46	```
47	
48	## Conventions worth knowing
49	
50	- **Logging.** `core.py` and every other library module use
51	  `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and never configure anything. Only entry points
52	  call `_log.configure()`. A library that calls `loguru.logger.add()` hijacks
53	  the logging of every program that imports it.
54	- **Commands are data.** Each subcommand is a frozen dataclass with a `run()`
55	  returning an exit code, so tests exercise it without parsing argv.
56	- **Exit codes.** `0` success, `1` unexpected error, `2` usage error (tyro),
57	  `4` validation error. Documented in `src/PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/cli/__init__.py`
58	  and asserted in `tests/test_cli.py`.
59	- **No `just`?** Every recipe is a plain `uv run ...`. The
60	  [taskipy](https://github.com/taskipy/taskipy) alternative puts the same
61	  commands under `[tool.taskipy.tasks]` in `pyproject.toml`, at the cost of a
62	  runtime dependency that cannot run before the environment exists.
63	
64	## After changing the CLI
65	
66	Command names, flags, defaults, and docstrings are documented below from
67	`--help`. Regenerate and commit:

71	```

73	`just check` runs `just docs-check`, which fails when this block is stale.

# Python release policy + PR-safe release ownership (#40 / #41)

## Context

The user wants to implement `.specstory/references/chatgpt-版本發布管理想法-20261102-0053.md` in the existing Python project skill and resolve GitHub issues #40 and #41. The motivating failure is parallel feature agents claiming stable versions/tags before main integrates their work; out-of-order and squash merges then cause version rollback or tags unrelated to the released main commit.

Issue #40 establishes the packaging baseline: `pyproject.toml` as the default single version source, explicit pre-1.0 compatibility policy, changelog scaffolding, release verification, and downstream pinning. Issue #41 propagates a PR-safe, main-centered, release-on-demand contract across Python/Git skills, generated agent instructions, and optional CI guardrails. Existing packaging backends remain supported; no forced VCS migration.

### Skill intent
- **Does:** teach and scaffold consistent Python version/release practice with explicit ownership boundaries.
- **Triggers:** Python project scaffolding/auditing, version/changelog changes, release preparation, concurrent worktree/PR development.
- **Outputs:** updated existing skills/references, generated project templates, focused guardrails and regression tests.
- **Verification:** deterministic scaffold tests, build/install metadata checks, negative policy cases, skill lint, repository publish gates.

## Recommended direction

1. Feature PRs change code and `[Unreleased]`, not stable versions, dated release headings, stable tags, or published packages. Ordinary CI may build unpublished verification artifacts.
2. Main integrates independently of release timing. An explicitly authorized release entry point owns version selection, changelog finalization, verification, immutable tags, and optional publishing.
3. Default new projects to static `[project].version`; support existing Hatch path-based versions and deliberate VCS-derived setups without competing sources of truth.
4. Keep policy summaries in skill entry points/generated AGENTS; detailed packaging mechanics in Python references and tag/provenance rules in Git references.
5. Add focused, tested verification/guardrail examples, not a new release automation platform or automatic publishing pipeline.

## Scope boundaries

- No changes to quant-data-kit, its tags, config CLI, or other downstream projects.
- No new skill, discovery symlinks, or marketplace regrouping.
- No real release, tag rewrite/deletion, package publication, automatic issue closure, commit, or push as part of implementation without the required authorization.
- Preserve current untracked SpecStory histories and the source conversation.

## Execution setup (after approval)

- Reuse `skills/local/forge-native-dev/scripts/forge-worktree.sh start 40` for isolated work. Treat #40/#41 as one cohesive change because they modify the same policy/templates; eventual PR should link both issues.

````text
1	# The agent interface: AGENTS.md, the self-skill, and the drift gate
2	
3	Load this when writing AGENTS.md, adding the package's own skill, or wiring the
4	check that stops those docs from going stale.
5	
6	## Three artifacts, three audiences
7	
8	| File | Audience | Answers |
9	|---|---|---|
10	| `README.md` | a human evaluating or installing | what is this, how do I install and run it |
11	| `AGENTS.md` | an agent working *in* this repo | how do I change this code correctly |
12	| `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | an agent *using* the tool elsewhere | how do I drive this CLI |
13	
14	They overlap in content and differ in purpose. Do not merge them: the README
15	gets read by someone deciding whether to try the tool, AGENTS.md by something
16	about to edit it.
17	
18	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
19	
20	Write one real file and symlink the other:
21	
22	```bash
23	ln -sf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
24	```
25	
26	`AGENTS.md` is the cross-agent convention (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Code
27	all read it or its symlink), so make that the real file. The direction is
28	arbitrary as long as exactly one is a symlink — *this* skills repo happens to
29	use the reverse.
30	
31	Never replace the symlink with a real file. Git stores it as mode `120000`;
32	two real files drift within a week and only one of them will be right. On a
33	Windows checkout without symlink support the link materializes as a text file
34	containing the path `AGENTS.md`, which looks like corruption — that is what it
35	is, and re-creating the symlink fixes it.
36	
37	## What belongs in AGENTS.md
38	
39	Only things an agent would otherwise get wrong. Not a tutorial.
40	
41	- **The command surface.** "Use `just`; `just --list` is complete." An agent
42	  that has to infer commands from CI config will infer them wrong.
43	- **Prohibitions with reasons.** "Never `pip install` — `uv sync` erases it."
44	  A rule without a reason gets rationalized away.
45	- **Layout, one line per directory**, including which direction imports flow.
46	- **Non-obvious conventions.** Where logging is configured and why library
47	  modules must not; the exit-code contract; where a new setting has to be
48	  added (`settings.py` *and* `.env.example`).
49	- **The definition of done.** `just check` [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es.
50	
51	Leave out anything the code already states plainly. Every line costs context on
52	every request.
53	
54	## The package's own skill
55	
56	Ship `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` inside the repo. Two payoffs: agents
57	working in *this* repo pick it up from the filesystem, and downstream users get
58	it in the same install as the code — the tool and its instructions version
59	together, so an agent never reads last release's flags.
60	
61	It should carry what a caller needs and nothing more: install line, exit-code
62	table, the stdout/stderr split, how to add a subcommand, and the generated CLI
63	reference.
64	
65	Frontmatter `description` is always-on context for every agent that loads the
66	skill. Make it name concrete trigger situations, keep it in the 120–500
67	character range, and **quote it** if it contains `:` or `#` — an unquoted YAML
68	scalar containing `": "` makes loaders drop the skill silently. See the
69	`skill-author` skill for the full authoring rules.
70	
71	## The drift gate
72	
73	Prose about a CLI rots the first time someone renames a flag. Generate it
74	instead:
75	
76	```bash
77	just docs-sync     # rewrite the block between the CLI markers from --help
78	just docs-check    # exit 1 if the committed block is stale  (part of `just check`)
79	```
80	
81	`scripts/sync_agent_docs.py` runs `python -m <pkg>.cli --help` plus each
82	subcommand's `--help`, strips ANSI, and splices the result between
83	`<!-- BEGIN CLI -->` and `<!-- END CLI -->` in every target file. Because
84	`--check` is in `just check` and in CI, a flag rename that skips the docs fails
85	the build. The docs become a build artifact with a test, rather than prose
86	someone has to remember.
87	
88	Two details that make it deterministic: force `NO_COLOR=1` and a fixed
89	`COLUMNS`, or the block churns depending on whose terminal ran it.
90	
91	## Recommended companion skills
92	
93	Print these in the scaffolder's `next_steps[]` and list them in AGENTS.md.
94	Do not vendor copies into the project — copies go stale and there is no update
95	path. One install line covers all of them:
96	
97	```bash
98	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
99	```
100	
101	| Always | Why |
102	|---|---|
103	| `project-knowledge-harness` | `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/` so deferred work and past traps survive the session |
104	| `agent-history-hygiene` | commit agent transcripts and plans with the diff, without leaking `.env` |
105	| `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` | GitHub Pages docs for humans, `llms.txt` for agents |
106	| `verifiable-surfaces` | the `--help` / `--dry-run` / exit-code discipline this layout assumes |
107	| `git-workflow` | Conventional Commits and AI-provenance trailers |
108	
109	| By project type | |
110	|---|---|
111	| ML | `mlflow-tracking`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `experiment-knowledge-harness`, `marimo-batch-mlflow` |
112	| HTTP service | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
113	| Library for others | `cli-release-distribution` (its Python section is `uv tool install` / PyPI) |
114
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Quality gates: ruff, types, pytest, CI
2	
3	Load this when configuring lint/format/type/test tooling, setting up CI, or
4	deciding what `just check` should contain.
5	
6	## One gate, four rungs
7	
8	`just check` = `fmt-check` → `lint-check` → `types` → `test` → `docs-check`,
9	ordered so the cheapest failure comes first. CI runs the same commands. If a
10	check exists only in CI, contributors discover it after pushing; if it exists
11	only locally, it stops being true.
12	
13	## ruff does lint AND format
14	
15	```toml
16	[tool.ruff]
17	line-length = 100
18	target-version = "py311"
19	src = ["src", "tests"]
20	
21	[tool.ruff.lint]
22	select = ["E", "W", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4", "RUF"]
23	```
24	
25	- `I` replaces isort, `UP` modernizes syntax to your `target-version`, `B`
26	  catches real bugs (mutable defaults, loop-variable capture), `SIM` and `C4`
27	  simplify, `RUF` is ruff's own set.
28	- **Do not also install black.** `ruff format` is a reimplementation of black's
29	  algorithm; running both means two tools rewriting the same file, disagreeing
30	  over magic trailing commas and string quoting. Pick ruff.
31	- `target-version` should equal your `requires-python` floor, not your
32	  development pin. `UP` rewrites to the *lowest* version you claim to support.
33	
34	Per-file ignores earn their keep in exactly two places:
35	
36	```toml
37	[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
38	"notebooks/*" = ["E402", "F401", "B018"]   # marimo cells are not linear scripts
39	"tests/*" = ["S101"]                        # only if you enable flake8-bandit
40	```
41	
42	## Type checking
43	
44	Two defensible defaults:
45	
46	| | `ty` | `mypy` |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| Speed | very fast (Rust, incremental) | slow on large trees |
49	| Maturity | **0.0.x, pre-1.0** — diagnostics change between patch releases | stable, a decade of edge cases |
50	| Editor | ships a language server | via pylsp/pyright |
51	
52	The template defaults to `ty` and pins it, because a type checker that reruns
53	in under a second is one people actually run. Pin it *exactly* — `ty==0.0.74`,
54	not `>=` — or a routine `uv lock --upgrade` will change what your gate accepts.
55	
56	Switch to mypy by replacing the dev dependency and the `just types` recipe:
57	
58	```toml
59	[tool.mypy]
60	strict = true
61	files = ["src", "tests"]
62	```
63	
64	Whichever you pick: ship `py.typed` in the package. Without that marker, a
65	consumer's type checker ignores every annotation you wrote.
66	
67	Compiled extensions are invisible to both. A PyO3 module needs a hand-written
68	`.pyi` next to it or the checker reports `has no member`; see
69	[`rust-pyo3.md`](rust-pyo3.md).
70	
71	## pytest layout
72	
73	```
74	src/my_tool/core.py
75	tests/test_core.py        # mirrors src/, module for module
76	```
77	
78	Tests live outside `src/`. With a src layout, `uv run pytest` imports the
79	*installed* package, so a missing `__init__.py`, a missing `py.typed`, or
80	un-shipped package data fails in your test run instead of in a user's install.
81	A flat layout imports the working directory and hides all three.
82	
83	```toml
84	[tool.pytest.ini_options]
85	addopts = "-q --strict-markers --strict-config"
86	testpaths = ["tests"]
87	```
88	
89	Keep coverage out of `addopts`. Always-on coverage slows every run, breaks
90	debugger attach, and trains people to ignore the number. Put it in one recipe
91	and in CI:
92	
93	```bash
94	uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80
95	```
96	
97	## TDD, and why it is the loop that works with agents
98	
99	Write the failing test first, then the code that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es it. With an agent in
100	the loop this stops being a style preference: the test is the only part of the
101	exchange that is machine-checkable. "Make the tests [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]" is a verifiable
102	instruction; "implement the feature" is not.
103	
104	Practical shape:
105	
106	1. Write the test. Run it. **Confirm it fails, and for the stated reason** — a
107	   test that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es before the implementation exists is testing nothing.
108	2. Implement the smallest change that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es it.
109	3. `just check`.
110	4. Refactor with the gate green.
111	
112	For the discipline itself — how to pick the next test, when to stub, how to
113	avoid tests that encode the implementation — use the vendored
114	`engineering-fundamentals/tdd` skill. This section only covers the mechanics.
115	
116	## CI
117	
118	```yaml
119	- uses: actions/checkout@v5
120	- uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10
121	  with:
122	    enable-cache: true
123	    python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
124	- run: uv sync --locked        # fails on a stale lock instead of re-resolving
125	- run: uv run ruff format --check .
126	- run: uv run ruff check .
127	- run: uv run ty check
128	- run: uv run pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80
129	```
130	
131	Notes worth the line each:
132	
133	- `--locked`, not plain `uv sync`. Without it, CI silently resolves a different
134	  dependency set than your machine and the lockfile stops meaning anything.
135	- Matrix the `requires-python` floor and the `.python-version` pin. Testing
136	  only the pin means your declared floor is untested.
137	- Pin actions to a release tag, or a commit SHA if you want supply-chain
138	  hardening. `@master` is a remote-code-execution surface you do not control.
139	- Action majors move. Check the current one rather than copying an old
140	  workflow — `setup-uv` was on v6 not long ago.
141	
142	## pre-commit
143	
144	Useful for the fast rungs (format, lint, secret detection) so bad commits never
145	land. Do not duplicate the whole gate there — a pre-commit hook that runs the
146	test suite gets by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed with `-n` within a week.
147	
148	The `agent-history-hygiene` skill already bootstraps pre-commit with secret
149	scanning; add ruff hooks to that config rather than starting a second one.
150
````
</details></tool-use>
