1	# The agent interface: AGENTS.md, the self-skill, and the drift gate
2	
3	Load this when writing AGENTS.md, adding the package's own skill, or wiring the
4	check that stops those docs from going stale.
5	
6	## Three artifacts, three audiences
7	
8	| File | Audience | Answers |
9	|---|---|---|
10	| `README.md` | a human evaluating or installing | what is this, how do I install and run it |
11	| `AGENTS.md` | an agent working *in* this repo | how do I change this code correctly |
12	| `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | an agent *using* the tool elsewhere | how do I drive this CLI |
13	
14	They overlap in content and differ in purpose. Do not merge them: the README
15	gets read by someone deciding whether to try the tool, AGENTS.md by something
16	about to edit it.
17	
18	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
19	
20	Write one real file and symlink the other:
21	
22	```bash
23	ln -sf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
24	```
25	
26	`AGENTS.md` is the cross-agent convention (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Code
27	all read it or its symlink), so make that the real file. The direction is
28	arbitrary as long as exactly one is a symlink — *this* skills repo happens to
29	use the reverse.
30	
31	Never replace the symlink with a real file. Git stores it as mode `120000`;
32	two real files drift within a week and only one of them will be right. On a
33	Windows checkout without symlink support the link materializes as a text file
34	containing the path `AGENTS.md`, which looks like corruption — that is what it
35	is, and re-creating the symlink fixes it.
36	
37	## What belongs in AGENTS.md
38	
39	Only things an agent would otherwise get wrong. Not a tutorial.
40	
41	- **The command surface.** "Use `just`; `just --list` is complete." An agent
42	  that has to infer commands from CI config will infer them wrong.
43	- **Prohibitions with reasons.** "Never `pip install` — `uv sync` erases it."
44	  A rule without a reason gets rationalized away.
45	- **Layout, one line per directory**, including which direction imports flow.
46	- **Non-obvious conventions.** Where logging is configured and why library
47	  modules must not; the exit-code contract; where a new setting has to be
48	  added (`settings.py` *and* `.env.example`).
49	- **The definition of done.** `just check` [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es.
50	
51	Leave out anything the code already states plainly. Every line costs context on
52	every request.
53	
54	## The package's own skill
55	
56	Ship `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` inside the repo. Two payoffs: agents
57	working in *this* repo pick it up from the filesystem, and downstream users get
58	it in the same install as the code — the tool and its instructions version
59	together, so an agent never reads last release's flags.
60	
61	It should carry what a caller needs and nothing more: install line, exit-code
62	table, the stdout/stderr split, how to add a subcommand, and the generated CLI
63	reference.
64	
65	Frontmatter `description` is always-on context for every agent that loads the
66	skill. Make it name concrete trigger situations, keep it in the 120–500
67	character range, and **quote it** if it contains `:` or `#` — an unquoted YAML
68	scalar containing `": "` makes loaders drop the skill silently. See the
69	`skill-author` skill for the full authoring rules.
70	
71	## The drift gate
72	
73	Prose about a CLI rots the first time someone renames a flag. Generate it
74	instead:
75	
76	```bash
77	just docs-sync     # rewrite the block between the CLI markers from --help
78	just docs-check    # exit 1 if the committed block is stale  (part of `just check`)
79	```
80	
81	`scripts/sync_agent_docs.py` runs `python -m <pkg>.cli --help` plus each
82	subcommand's `--help`, strips ANSI, and splices the result between
83	`<!-- BEGIN CLI -->` and `<!-- END CLI -->` in every target file. Because
84	`--check` is in `just check` and in CI, a flag rename that skips the docs fails
85	the build. The docs become a build artifact with a test, rather than prose
86	someone has to remember.
87	
88	Two details that make it deterministic: force `NO_COLOR=1` and a fixed
89	`COLUMNS`, or the block churns depending on whose terminal ran it.
90	
91	## Recommended companion skills
92	
93	Print these in the scaffolder's `next_steps[]` and list them in AGENTS.md.
94	Do not vendor copies into the project — copies go stale and there is no update
95	path. One install line covers all of them:
96	
97	```bash
98	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
99	```
100	
101	| Always | Why |
102	|---|---|
103	| `project-knowledge-harness` | `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/` so deferred work and past traps survive the session |
104	| `agent-history-hygiene` | commit agent transcripts and plans with the diff, without leaking `.env` |
105	| `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` | GitHub Pages docs for humans, `llms.txt` for agents |
106	| `verifiable-surfaces` | the `--help` / `--dry-run` / exit-code discipline this layout assumes |
107	| `git-workflow` | Conventional Commits and AI-provenance trailers |
108	
109	| By project type | |
110	|---|---|
111	| ML | `mlflow-tracking`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `experiment-knowledge-harness`, `marimo-batch-mlflow` |
112	| HTTP service | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
113	| Library for others | `cli-release-distribution` (its Python section is `uv tool install` / PyPI) |
114
````

````text
1	# Quality gates: ruff, types, pytest, CI
2	
3	Load this when configuring lint/format/type/test tooling, setting up CI, or
4	deciding what `just check` should contain.
5	
6	## One gate, four rungs
7	
8	`just check` = `fmt-check` → `lint-check` → `types` → `test` → `docs-check`,
9	ordered so the cheapest failure comes first. CI runs the same commands. If a
10	check exists only in CI, contributors discover it after pushing; if it exists
11	only locally, it stops being true.
12	
13	## ruff does lint AND format
14	
15	```toml
16	[tool.ruff]
17	line-length = 100
18	target-version = "py311"
19	src = ["src", "tests"]
20	
21	[tool.ruff.lint]
22	select = ["E", "W", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4", "RUF"]
23	```
24	
25	- `I` replaces isort, `UP` modernizes syntax to your `target-version`, `B`
26	  catches real bugs (mutable defaults, loop-variable capture), `SIM` and `C4`
27	  simplify, `RUF` is ruff's own set.
28	- **Do not also install black.** `ruff format` is a reimplementation of black's
29	  algorithm; running both means two tools rewriting the same file, disagreeing
30	  over magic trailing commas and string quoting. Pick ruff.
31	- `target-version` should equal your `requires-python` floor, not your
32	  development pin. `UP` rewrites to the *lowest* version you claim to support.
33	
34	Per-file ignores earn their keep in exactly two places:
35	
36	```toml
37	[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
38	"notebooks/*" = ["E402", "F401", "B018"]   # marimo cells are not linear scripts
39	"tests/*" = ["S101"]                        # only if you enable flake8-bandit
40	```
41	
42	## Type checking
43	
44	Two defensible defaults:
45	
46	| | `ty` | `mypy` |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| Speed | very fast (Rust, incremental) | slow on large trees |
49	| Maturity | **0.0.x, pre-1.0** — diagnostics change between patch releases | stable, a decade of edge cases |
50	| Editor | ships a language server | via pylsp/pyright |
51	
52	The template defaults to `ty` and pins it, because a type checker that reruns
53	in under a second is one people actually run. Pin it *exactly* — `ty==0.0.74`,
54	not `>=` — or a routine `uv lock --upgrade` will change what your gate accepts.
55	
56	Switch to mypy by replacing the dev dependency and the `just types` recipe:
57	
58	```toml
59	[tool.mypy]
60	strict = true
61	files = ["src", "tests"]
62	```
63	
64	Whichever you pick: ship `py.typed` in the package. Without that marker, a
65	consumer's type checker ignores every annotation you wrote.
66	
67	Compiled extensions are invisible to both. A PyO3 module needs a hand-written
68	`.pyi` next to it or the checker reports `has no member`; see
69	[`rust-pyo3.md`](rust-pyo3.md).
70	
71	## pytest layout
72	
73	```
74	src/my_tool/core.py
75	tests/test_core.py        # mirrors src/, module for module
76	```
77	
78	Tests live outside `src/`. With a src layout, `uv run pytest` imports the
79	*installed* package, so a missing `__init__.py`, a missing `py.typed`, or
80	un-shipped package data fails in your test run instead of in a user's install.
81	A flat layout imports the working directory and hides all three.
82	
83	```toml
84	[tool.pytest.ini_options]
85	addopts = "-q --strict-markers --strict-config"
86	testpaths = ["tests"]
87	```
88	
89	Keep coverage out of `addopts`. Always-on coverage slows every run, breaks
90	debugger attach, and trains people to ignore the number. Put it in one recipe
91	and in CI:
92	
93	```bash
94	uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80
95	```
96	
97	## TDD, and why it is the loop that works with agents
98	
99	Write the failing test first, then the code that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es it. With an agent in
100	the loop this stops being a style preference: the test is the only part of the
101	exchange that is machine-checkable. "Make the tests [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]" is a verifiable
102	instruction; "implement the feature" is not.
103	
104	Practical shape:
105	
106	1. Write the test. Run it. **Confirm it fails, and for the stated reason** — a
107	   test that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es before the implementation exists is testing nothing.
108	2. Implement the smallest change that [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es it.
109	3. `just check`.
110	4. Refactor with the gate green.
111	
112	For the discipline itself — how to pick the next test, when to stub, how to
113	avoid tests that encode the implementation — use the vendored
114	`engineering-fundamentals/tdd` skill. This section only covers the mechanics.
115	
116	## CI
117	
118	```yaml
119	- uses: actions/checkout@v5
120	- uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10
121	  with:
122	    enable-cache: true
123	    python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
124	- run: uv sync --locked        # fails on a stale lock instead of re-resolving
125	- run: uv run ruff format --check .
126	- run: uv run ruff check .
127	- run: uv run ty check
128	- run: uv run pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80
129	```
130	
131	Notes worth the line each:
132	
133	- `--locked`, not plain `uv sync`. Without it, CI silently resolves a different
134	  dependency set than your machine and the lockfile stops meaning anything.
135	- Matrix the `requires-python` floor and the `.python-version` pin. Testing
136	  only the pin means your declared floor is untested.
137	- Pin actions to a release tag, or a commit SHA if you want supply-chain
138	  hardening. `@master` is a remote-code-execution surface you do not control.
139	- Action majors move. Check the current one rather than copying an old
140	  workflow — `setup-uv` was on v6 not long ago.
141	
142	## pre-commit
143	
144	Useful for the fast rungs (format, lint, secret detection) so bad commits never
145	land. Do not duplicate the whole gate there — a pre-commit hook that runs the
146	test suite gets by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed with `-n` within a week.
147	
148	The `agent-history-hygiene` skill already bootstraps pre-commit with secret
149	scanning; add ruff hooks to that config rather than starting a second one.
150
````

1	# scripts/
2	
3	Repo helpers that are **not** part of the shipped package. Nothing in
4	`src/PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/` may import from here.
5	
6	Two kinds live here, and the distinction decides how you write the file:
7	
8	| Kind | How it runs | Dependencies |
9	|---|---|---|
10	| Needs the project | `uv run python scripts/foo.py` | the project env (`uv.lock`) |
11	| Standalone | `uv run scripts/foo.py` | its own PEP 723 header |
12	
13	A standalone helper declares its dependencies inline, so it works in a fresh
14	clone before `uv sync` has ever run:
15	
16	```python
17	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
18	# /// script
19	# requires-python = ">=PYTHON_FLOOR_PLACEHOLDER"
20	# dependencies = ["httpx>=0.28"]
21	# ///
22	```
23	
24	A PEP 723 script must not `import PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER` unless the package
25	is listed in its own `dependencies` - it runs in an isolated environment that
26	does not contain your project.
27	
28	Anything worth running twice gets a `just` recipe so it shows up in
29	`just --list`.
30
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Versioning & releases
2	
3	Read this when cutting a release, tagging a version, or wiring a Python package
4	so its version comes from the git tag. Covers [SemVer](https://semver.org/),
5	annotated tags, and tag-driven Python versioning.
6	
7	## Table of contents
8	
9	1. [SemVer in one paragraph](#semver-in-one-paragraph)
10	2. [Mapping commits to bumps](#mapping-commits-to-bumps)
11	3. [Tagging a release](#tagging-a-release)
12	4. [When to tag](#when-to-tag)
13	5. [Python: git tag as single source of truth](#python-git-tag-as-single-source-of-truth)
14	6. [Changelog](#changelog)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## SemVer in one paragraph
19	
20	`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Bump **MAJOR** for incompatible API changes, **MINOR** for
21	backward-compatible features, **PATCH** for backward-compatible fixes.
22	Pre-release and build metadata append as `-rc.1` / `+build.5`
23	(e.g. `2.0.0-rc.1`). Below `1.0.0` anything may change; `1.0.0` is the
24	commitment to a stable public API.
25	
26	## Mapping commits to bumps
27	
28	If commits follow [Conventional Commits](conventional-commits.md), the bump is
29	mechanical:
30	
31	- `fix:` / `perf:` → PATCH
32	- `feat:` → MINOR
33	- `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` → MAJOR
34	
35	Tools like [`commitizen`](https://commitizen-tools.github.io/commitizen/) or
36	`semantic-release` can compute the next version and changelog from the log.
37	
38	## Tagging a release
39	
40	Use an **annotated**, `v`-prefixed tag on the release commit:
41	
42	```bash
43	git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "release: v1.4.0"
44	git push origin v1.4.0
45	# or push commits + their tags together:
46	git commit ... && git push --follow-tags
47	```
48	
49	- **Annotated** (`-a`) tags store tagger, date, and message and are the right
50	  choice for releases (lightweight tags are just a moving label).
51	- Create the tag **on the commit that is the release** — don't tag ahead of it.
52	  Fixing a mis-placed tag means `git tag -f` + a force-push of the tag, which
53	  is disruptive if others already fetched it.
54	- List/inspect: `git tag --list 'v1.*'`, `git show v1.4.0`.
55	
56	## When to tag
57	
58	- **Applications/services**: at each deploy boundary worth returning to, or per
59	  release train (`v2025.07.0`-style calendar versions are also fine if that's
60	  your convention).
61	- **Libraries/packages**: at every published version — the tag *is* the release
62	  users depend on.
63	- Tag from `main` (Tier 3) or the promoted release commit (Tier 2). Don't tag
64	  arbitrary WIP commits.
65	
66	## Python: git tag as single source of truth
67	
68	When the whole repo **is** a Python package, don't hand-maintain a version
69	string in `__init__.py` *and* `pyproject.toml` *and* a git tag — derive it from
70	the tag. See the [Python Packaging guide on single-sourcing the version](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/).
71	
72	**setuptools backend** — [setuptools-scm](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/):
73	
74	```toml
75	[build-system]
76	requires = ["setuptools>=64", "setuptools-scm>=8"]
77	build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
78	
79	[project]
80	name = "yourpkg"
81	dynamic = ["version"]
82	
83	[tool.setuptools_scm]
84	# version comes from the latest git tag; a dev suffix is added between tags
85	```
86	
87	**Hatch backend** — [hatch-vcs](https://pypi.org/project/hatch-vcs/):
88	
89	```toml
90	[build-system]
91	requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
92	build-backend = "hatchling.build"
93	
94	[project]
95	name = "yourpkg"
96	dynamic = ["version"]
97	
98	[tool.hatch.version]
99	source = "vcs"
100	```
101	
102	Notes:
103	- Tags must be **PEP 440-compatible** once parsed. `vX.Y.Z` works (the `v` is
104	  stripped); avoid tags that don't map to PEP 440.
105	- Version is resolved at **build/install time**. Editable/dev installs can show
106	  a stale value until rebuilt — expected behavior, not a bug.
107	- In CI, cut the release by pushing the tag; the build then stamps the matching
108	  version. Verify the tag produces the expected version in CI before publishing.
109	
110	## Changelog
111	
112	Keep a human-readable `CHANGELOG.md` (the
113	[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) format is a good default), or
114	generate it from Conventional Commits with `commitizen`/`semantic-release`.
115	Either way, the changelog entry and the tag should agree on the version.
116
````
</details></tool-use>

````text
1	# Worktrees for parallel agents
2	
3	Read this before setting up parallel Claude Code sessions/agents, or when
4	debugging a worktree that's missing a gitignored file (like `.env`) or won't
5	clean up. Based on the official
6	[Claude Code worktrees docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees) and
7	[`git worktree`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree).
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [Why worktrees](#why-worktrees)
12	2. [Starting a worktree](#starting-a-worktree)
13	3. [Choosing the base branch](#choosing-the-base-branch)
14	4. [Copying gitignored files (`.worktreeinclude`)](#copying-gitignored-files-worktreeinclude)
15	5. [Isolating subagents](#isolating-subagents)
16	6. [SpecStory separation bonus](#specstory-separation-bonus)
17	7. [Cleanup](#cleanup)
18	8. [Manual worktrees & non-git VCS](#manual-worktrees--non-git-vcs)
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Why worktrees
23	
24	A git worktree is a separate working directory with its own files and branch,
25	sharing the same repo history and remote. Running each parallel agent/session
26	in its own worktree means edits in one never touch another — one terminal
27	builds a feature while a second fixes a bug, with zero file collisions.
28	
29	## Starting a worktree
30	
31	```bash
32	claude --worktree feature-auth   # or -w
33	# → creates .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/ on branch worktree-feature-auth
34	claude --worktree                # omit the name → generates e.g. bright-running-fox
35	```
36	
37	You can also ask Claude to "work in a worktree" mid-session (it uses the
38	`EnterWorktree` tool). **Add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore`** so worktree
39	contents don't appear as untracked files in your main checkout.
40	
41	## Choosing the base branch
42	
43	- Default: worktrees branch from `origin/HEAD` (your default branch), so they
44	  start from a clean tree matching the remote.
45	- To branch from your **local HEAD** (carrying unpushed commits / feature-branch
46	  state — useful for isolating subagents on in-progress work), set in settings:
47	
48	```json
49	{ "worktree": { "baseRef": "head" } }
50	```
51	
52	  Only `"fresh"` (default) or `"head"` are accepted — not arbitrary refs.
53	- Branch from a specific PR: `claude --worktree "#1234"` →
54	  `.claude/worktrees/pr-1234`.
55	
56	## Copying gitignored files (`.worktreeinclude`)
57	
58	A worktree is a fresh checkout, so untracked files like `.env` are **not**
59	present. Add a `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root to copy them in
60	automatically. It uses `.gitignore` syntax and copies **only files that match a
61	pattern *and* are gitignored** — tracked files are never duplicated.
62	
63	```text
64	# .worktreeinclude — gitignored files to carry into new worktrees
65	.env
66	.env.local
67	config/secrets.json
68	```
69	
70	**Key correction to a common misconception:** a committed
71	`.vscode/settings.json` is *tracked*, so it's already in the worktree checkout
72	— listing it here does nothing. Only put genuinely-ignored files here. Applies
73	to `--worktree`, subagent worktrees, and desktop parallel sessions.
74	
75	## Isolating subagents
76	
77	Give parallel subagents their own worktrees so their edits don't conflict:
78	
79	- Ask Claude to "use worktrees for your agents", or
80	- set it permanently on a custom subagent with frontmatter:
81	
82	```yaml
83	---
84	name: my-agent
85	isolation: worktree
86	---
87	```
88	
89	Each subagent gets a temporary worktree, removed automatically when it finishes
90	without changes. Subagent worktrees use the same base branch as `--worktree`.
91	
92	## SpecStory separation bonus
93	
94	SpecStory tracks transcripts by **directory**, not branch. Because each
95	worktree is a fresh directory, parallel agents each accumulate their chat
96	history under their own `.specstory/` — a clean cut that avoids interleaving
97	transcripts from concurrent sessions.
98	
99	## Cleanup
100	
101	On exiting a worktree session:
102	
103	- **No changes/commits**: worktree + branch removed automatically (named
104	  sessions prompt so you can keep them).
105	- **Uncommitted changes / untracked / new commits**: Claude prompts to keep or
106	  remove.
107	- **Non-interactive `-p` runs**: not cleaned up automatically — remove with
108	  `git worktree remove` (add `--force` if it has uncommitted work).
109	
110	Subagent/background worktrees are swept once older than `cleanupPeriodDays`,
111	provided they have no uncommitted changes/untracked files/unpushed commits.
112	
113	## Manual worktrees & non-git VCS
114	
115	Full manual control:
116	
117	```bash
118	git worktree add ../proj-feature-a -b feature-a   # new branch
119	git worktree add ../proj-bugfix bugfix-123        # existing branch
120	git worktree list
121	git worktree remove ../proj-feature-a
122	```
123	
124	Remember to reinitialize the dev environment in each new worktree (install
125	deps, create venvs). For **non-git VCS** (SVN/Perforce/hg), configure
126	`WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks — note that `.worktreeinclude` is **not
127	processed** when a custom hook replaces the default git logic, so copy local
128	config files inside the hook script instead.
129	
130	## Worktrees in a submodule superproject
131	
132	A worktree of a **superproject** starts with every submodule uninitialized, so
133	it is the wrong tool for work inside a child repo. Create a worktree of the
134	**child** instead, under `.worktrees/<child-path>/<branch>`. The
135	`superproject-workspace` skill's
136	`superproject.py worktree add <child> <branch>` does this, including the
137	`.gitignore` entry and branching pins from their recorded gitlink. See its
138	`references/worktrees.md`.
139
````

````text
1	# Conventional Commits
2	
3	Read this when writing a non-trivial commit message, wiring
4	`scripts/check-commit-msg.sh`, or deciding how a change should bump the
5	version. This condenses the [Conventional Commits v1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
6	spec and the house rules for this workflow.
7	
8	## Table of contents
9	
10	1. [Format](#format)
11	2. [Types](#types)
12	3. [Scope](#scope)
13	4. [Subject line rules](#subject-line-rules)
14	5. [Body and footers](#body-and-footers)
15	6. [Agentic provenance](#agentic-provenance)
16	7. [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes)
17	8. [SemVer mapping](#semver-mapping)
18	9. [Examples](#examples)
19	10. [The English rule](#the-english-rule)
20	11. [Tooling](#tooling)
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Format
25	
26	```
27	<type>[(scope)][!]: <subject>
28	
29	[body]
30	
31	[footer(s)]
32	```
33	
34	Only the first line (`<type>: <subject>`) is mandatory. A blank line separates
35	header, body, and footers.
36	
37	## Types
38	
39	| Type | Use for | SemVer |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| `feat` | a new user-facing feature | MINOR |
42	| `fix` | a bug fix | PATCH |
43	| `docs` | documentation only | — |
44	| `style` | formatting/whitespace, no code-behavior change | — |
45	| `refactor` | code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature | — |
46	| `perf` | a performance improvement | PATCH |
47	| `test` | adding or fixing tests | — |
48	| `build` | build system, dependencies, packaging | — |
49	| `ci` | CI configuration and scripts | — |
50	| `chore` | maintenance that doesn't touch src/test (e.g. `.gitignore`) | — |
51	| `revert` | reverts a previous commit | — |
52	
53	Keep to this set; consistency is the point. `perf` bumps PATCH because it
54	changes runtime behavior; `refactor` does not.
55	
56	## Scope
57	
58	Optional noun in parentheses naming the area touched: `feat(auth):`,
59	`fix(parser):`, `docs(readme):`. Use a short, stable vocabulary per repo
60	(module names, subsystems). Omit it when a change is broad or the repo is small.
61	
62	## Subject line rules
63	
64	- **Imperative mood**: "add", "fix", "remove" — as if completing *"This commit
65	  will …"*. Not "added"/"adds"/"adding".
66	- **Lowercase** first word; **no trailing period**.
67	- Keep the whole header **≤ ~72 characters** (50 is a good aim).
68	- Describe *what/why*, not *how*: `fix(client): retry on 429` beats
69	  `fix: change the loop`.
70	
71	## Body and footers
72	
73	- **Body** (optional): the *why* and any context that won't be obvious from the
74	  diff. Wrap at ~72 columns. Bullet lists are fine. For non-trivial commits
75	  produced with an agent harness, the body is required; include the outcome and
76	  meaningful validation, not a line-by-line diff recital.
77	- **Footers** (optional), one per line, `Key: value`:
78	  - `Refs: #123` / `Closes: #123` — issue linkage.
79	  - `Co-Authored-By: Name <email>` — native/human co-author attribution.
80	  - `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` — see below.
81	
82	## Agentic provenance
83	
84	Keep the human as Git author/committer and add a portable final trailer block:
85	
86	```text
87	AI-Assisted-By: Claude Code (Claude Fable 5)
88	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/2026-08-27_session.md
89	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/session.md
90	```
91	
92	- `AI-Assisted-By` always names both harness and model. Repeat it for distinct
93	  contributors; never use `unknown` or manufacture an AI email address.
94	- Artifact paths are repo-relative and must name files in the same commit.
95	- Native metadata such as Claude Code's `Co-Authored-By` is preserved. Put any
96	  Generated-with prose before the trailer block, and keep the canonical fields
97	  in the final block so `git interpret-trailers --parse` sees them.
98	- Message attribution and SSH/GPG signing are independent. A signature proves
99	  control of a key over the exact commit object; amending or squash-merging
100	  creates a different object and discards the original signature.
101	
102	## Breaking changes
103	
104	Two equivalent ways to mark an incompatible change (→ **MAJOR** bump):
105	
106	```
107	feat(api)!: drop v1 auth endpoints
108	
109	BREAKING CHANGE: /v1/auth is removed; migrate to /v2/token.
110	```
111	
112	The `!` after the type/scope is the quick signal; the `BREAKING CHANGE:`
113	footer carries the migration note. Either alone is valid; use both for clarity.
114	
115	## SemVer mapping
116	
117	The commit log becomes a changelog and a version driver (see
118	[`versioning-and-releases.md`](versioning-and-releases.md)):
119	
120	- `fix:` / `perf:` → **PATCH** (`1.2.3 → 1.2.4`)
121	- `feat:` → **MINOR** (`1.2.3 → 1.3.0`)
122	- any `!` / `BREAKING CHANGE:` → **MAJOR** (`1.2.3 → 2.0.0`)
123	- `docs`/`style`/`test`/`chore`/`ci`/`build`/`refactor` → no release on their own
124	
125	## Examples
126	
127	```
128	feat(worktree): copy gitignored env files via .worktreeinclude
129	fix(branch-status): treat squash-merged branches as gone, not active
130	docs(readme): add install one-liner
131	refactor(cli)!: rename --out to --output
132	
133	BREAKING CHANGE: the --out flag is removed; use --output.
134	revert: feat(auth): add token refresh
135	
136	This reverts commit 9fceb02.
137	
138	feat(agent-history): emit staged provenance trailers
139	
140	Derive harness, model, transcript, and plan metadata from the staged snapshot
141	so different coding-agent harnesses produce the same reviewable history.
142	
143	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
144	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
145	```
146	
147	## The English rule
148	
149	Commit messages, branch names, and tags are **English**, even when the prompt
150	or conversation is Chinese. Rationale: history is consumed by changelog/SemVer
151	tooling and future collaborators, and a mixed-language log is hard to grep and
152	automate. Translate the *intent* — don't transliterate the prompt. (Your PR
153	description or issue comments can be bilingual; the git object graph stays EN.)
154	
155	## Tooling
156	
157	- **This skill**: `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` keeps its header-only default;
158	  `--agentic --staged` validates the English description, canonical trailers,
159	  and artifact paths with agent-friendly exit codes.
160	- **Companion**: `agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh`
161	  derives the canonical trailer block from staged artifacts.
162	- **Escape hatch — enforce in-repo**: [`commitlint`](https://commitlint.js.org/)
163	  via a `commit-msg` hook, or [`commitizen`](https://commitizen-tools.github.io/commitizen/)
164	  for guided prompts + automated version bumps. Adopt these when a team needs
165	  hard enforcement; for solo work the template + validator are enough.
166	- **Template**: `assets/commit-template.txt` →
167	  `git config commit.template skills/local/git-workflow/assets/commit-template.txt`.
168
````

````text
1	# Project tiers — main vs dev vs PR
2	
3	Read this when deciding whether to commit straight to `main`, introduce a
4	`dev` branch, or move to a PR-based flow — or when a project outgrows its
5	current tier. The goal is to match ceremony to real collaboration needs, not
6	to a project's ambitions.
7	
8	## Table of contents
9	
10	1. [The promotion signal](#the-promotion-signal)
11	2. [Tier 1 — solo / early](#tier-1--solo--early)
12	3. [Tier 2 — prod/dev split](#tier-2--proddev-split)
13	4. [Tier 3 — team / grown vibe-coding](#tier-3--team--grown-vibe-coding)
14	5. [GitHub Flow in one screen](#github-flow-in-one-screen)
15	6. [Choosing a merge strategy](#choosing-a-merge-strategy)
16	
17	---
18	
19	## The promotion signal
20	
21	Don't adopt a heavier tier until the signal actually appears. Over-branching a
22	solo repo just adds friction; under-branching a shared repo causes collisions
23	and un-reviewable history.
24	
25	| Move to | When |
26	|---|---|
27	| Tier 2 | someone (a deploy, a teammate, "prod") depends on a stable line while you keep working |
28	| Tier 3 | a second contributor appears, **or** you want a per-feature review/CI gate even solo |
29	
30	You can also **skip** tiers: a solo vibe-coding project with heavy CI may go
31	straight to Tier 3, using PRs purely as a "ship a feature" boundary.
32	
33	## Tier 1 — solo / early
34	
35	One `main`. Commit directly; keep history linear.
36	
37	```bash
38	git config pull.rebase true
39	git config merge.ff only
40	
41	# work, commit in logical/phase-sized chunks
42	git add -p && git commit            # uses your commit.template
43	
44	# stay current without merge commits
45	git pull --rebase
46	
47	# optional short-lived branch, landed with no merge commit
48	git switch -c fix/typo
49	# ...commit...
50	git switch main && git merge --ff-only fix/typo && git branch -d fix/typo
51	```
52	
53	Tag releases when a state is worth returning to (see
54	[`versioning-and-releases.md`](versioning-and-releases.md)).
55	
56	## Tier 2 — prod/dev split
57	
58	`main` = last released/deployed state; `dev` = integration line. Feature
59	branches cut from `dev`, land on `dev`, and `dev` fast-forwards to `main` at a
60	release boundary.
61	
62	```bash
63	git switch dev && git pull --rebase
64	git switch -c feat/import-csv        # branch off dev
65	# ...commits...
66	git switch dev && git merge --ff-only feat/import-csv
67	
68	# release: promote dev to main
69	git switch main && git merge --ff-only dev
70	git tag -a v0.4.0 -m "release: v0.4.0" && git push --follow-tags
71	```
72	
73	Keep hotfixes on `main` and merge them back into `dev` so the lines don't
74	diverge. If `--ff-only` refuses (lines diverged), rebase `dev` onto `main`
75	first.
76	
77	## Tier 3 — team / grown vibe-coding
78	
79	`main` is always deployable. All work happens on short-lived branches that
80	merge via **pull request** after review + CI. This is
81	[GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow).
82	
83	```bash
84	git switch main && git pull --rebase
85	git switch -c feat/oauth             # or agent/oauth for agent work
86	# ...commits...
87	git push -u origin feat/oauth
88	gh pr create --fill                  # glab mr create --fill
89	gh pr checks                         # wait for CI
90	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch # collapse WIP into one clean commit
91	git switch main && git pull --rebase && git fetch --prune
92	```
93	
94	The PR is the unit of "a feature shipped": it isolates finished work from
95	in-progress work, gives CI a place to run, and (even solo) creates a reviewable
96	diff and a revert point.
97	
98	## GitHub Flow in one screen
99	
100	1. `main` is always deployable.
101	2. Branch off `main` with a descriptive name.
102	3. Commit and push; open a PR early for visibility.
103	4. Discuss/review; let CI run.
104	5. Merge to `main` (squash or rebase).
105	6. Deploy from `main`; delete the branch.
106	
107	## Choosing a merge strategy
108	
109	| Strategy | History effect | Best for |
110	|---|---|---|
111	| `--ff-only` | linear, no merge commit | solo/local landing of a clean branch |
112	| **squash-merge** | one commit per PR on `main` | vibe-coding branches with noisy WIP |
113	| **rebase-merge** | each commit preserved, linear | branches where every commit is already meaningful |
114	| `--no-ff` merge | explicit merge commit | when you want the branch topology recorded |
115	
116	Default here: `--ff-only` locally, **squash** for vibe-coding PRs, **rebase**
117	for curated PRs. Avoid default `--no-ff` merges unless the merge topology is
118	information you want to keep.
119
````

1	# python-project-best-practice
2	
3	An opinionated baseline for Python projects that both people and agents work
4	in — and the two entry points that get you there: **scaffold a new project**,
5	or **score and modernize an existing one**. Same conventions, one skill.
6	
7	The bias throughout: every operation has one canonical, discoverable,
8	non-interactive command. That is what makes a repo workable by an agent, and
9	it happens to be what makes it pleasant for humans.
10	
11	> Scope note: this skill deliberately does **not** restate
12	> [`verifiable-surfaces`](verifiable-surfaces.md) (CLI surface design),
13	> [`marimo-batch-mlflow`](marimo-batch-mlflow.md) (dual-mode notebooks),
14	> [`fastapi-ai-patterns`](fastapi-ai-patterns.md) (production FastAPI), or
15	> [`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`](mkdocs-site-bootstrap.md) (docs sites). It links
16	> to them and fills the gap none of them covered: the project itself.
17	
18	## The defaults it argues for
19	
20	| Concern | Default | Why not the alternative |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| Environment | `uv` + committed `uv.lock` + `.python-version` | poetry/pip-tools/conda all solve less of it; `uv.lock` never constrains your users |
23	| Layout | `src/<pkg>/` | a flat layout imports the source dir, so missing `__init__.py` / package data [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es tests and breaks installs |
24	| Dev deps | PEP 735 `[dependency-groups]` | an extra is **published**; your test runner should not be in your users' dependency graph |
25	| Lint + format | `ruff check` + `ruff format` | `ruff format` *is* a black reimplementation — running both makes them fight |
26	| Types | `ty` (pinned exactly), mypy documented as the conservative swap | `ty` is 0.0.x: fast enough that people run it, unstable enough that `>=` is a trap |
27	| CLI | Tyro, one frozen dataclass per subcommand | commands as data are testable without argv or subprocesses |
28	| Completion | `--tyro-write-completion` | built in; shtab/argcomplete wiring is redundant |
29	| Logging | loguru at entry points, stdlib in library code | a library that calls `loguru.logger.add()` hijacks the importing program's logging |
30	| Config | pydantic-settings, defaults < `.env` < environment | and `<tool> info` prints what actually resolved |
31	| Task runner | `Justfile` (taskipy noted) | `just` needs no Python, so `just setup` can bootstrap the venv itself |
32	
33	## What ships
34	
35	- The full SKILL.md ([SKILL.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/python-project-best-practice/SKILL.md)) — decision spine, two workflows,

71	
72	## Profiles
73	
74	Additive, so "agentic later" costs nothing now.
75	
76	| Profile | Adds |
77	|---|---|
78	| `minimal` | package, tests, Justfile, CI, AGENTS.md |
79	| `cli` *(default)* | Tyro CLI, loguru, pydantic-settings, `[project.scripts]` |
80	| `lib` | publishing metadata, `py.typed` |
81	| `api` | FastAPI app with `/docs` and `/openapi.json` |
82	| `ml` | a marimo notebook that is also a batch CLI |
83	| `rust` | maturin backend, PyO3 crate, `.pyi` stubs |
84	
85	## The docs-drift gate
86	
87	The piece worth stealing even if you use none of the rest. Prose about a CLI
88	rots the first time someone renames a flag, so the generated project makes it
89	a build artifact instead:
90	
91	```bash

````text
1	# git-workflow
2	
3	One opinionated, scale-aware git workflow that stays consistent from a solo
4	weekend repo to a multi-person, multi-month project — so commit messages,
5	branch names, merge strategy, and release tags stop being improvised per
6	project. Commits are **English and follow Conventional Commits**, even when the
7	prompt is in another language.
8	
9	| Surface | Question it answers |
10	|---|---|
11	| `references/project-tiers.md` | "Do I commit to `main`, use a `dev` branch, or open PRs?" |
12	| `references/conventional-commits.md` | "What goes in the commit message, including AI provenance?" |
13	| `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` | "How do I run parallel agents without collisions?" |
14	| `references/versioning-and-releases.md` | "When and how do I tag a version?" |
15	| `references/branch-hygiene.md` | "Which local branches are done vs still in-dev?" |
16	| `scripts/branch-status.sh` | The same, as data — classify every local branch. |
17	| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | "Is this commit message valid?" |
18	| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | "How do I do this in lazygit?" (learning aid) |
19	
20	If you want the *why* behind the defaults — the concepts, not the skill
21	mechanics — read the companion explainer:
22	[Git workflow best practices](../reference/git-workflow.md).
23	
24	## When the skill triggers
25	
26	- "Commit this" / "幫我 commit" / "整理一下 git" / "write a commit message".
27	- "Should I branch or just commit to main?" / "should I open a PR?".
28	- "Set up worktrees for parallel agents" / "carry my `.env` into the worktree".
29	- "How do I tag / release a version?" / "bump the version".
30	- "My local branches are a mess — which ones are done?" / "clean up branches".
31	- Starting a new repo and wanting one consistent commit/branch/release
32	  convention for you and your agents.
33	
34	## The three tiers
35	
36	Match ceremony to real collaboration needs; promote only when the signal
37	appears.
38	
39	| Tier | Shape | Branching | Integration |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| **1 — Solo / early** | one `main` | commit to `main`; short local branches optional | `pull --rebase`, `merge --ff-only` |
42	| **2 — prod/dev split** | `main` = released, `dev` = integration | feature branches off `dev` | merge to `dev`; ff `dev`→`main` at release |
43	| **3 — Team / grown vibe-coding** | `main` always deployable | short `feat/…` → PR | PR review/CI → squash-merge |
44	
45	A solo vibe-coding project can jump straight to Tier 3: the PR becomes the
46	"ship a feature" boundary and a place for CI to run, even with one human.
47	
48	## Defaults at a glance
49	
50	- **Commits**: English `type(scope): subject`; non-trivial agent commits add a
51	  why/outcome body plus `AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, and conditional
52	  `Agent-Plan` trailers. `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` drives a major bump.
53	- **History**: linear — `pull.rebase=true`, `merge.ff=only`; squash-merge noisy
54	  vibe-coding PRs, rebase-merge curated ones.
55	- **Branches**: `feat/ fix/ chore/ docs/ refactor/ exp/` for human intent,
56	  `agent/…` for agent/vibe work, `worktree-*` for Claude worktrees.
57	- **Worktrees**: `claude --worktree <name>`; `.worktreeinclude` (gitignored
58	  files only) to carry `.env` in; gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`.
59	- **Releases**: SemVer, annotated `v`-prefixed tags; for a Python package let
60	  the git tag drive the version (setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs).
61	- **Forge CLIs**: `gh` (GitHub) / `glab` (GitLab) for PRs from the terminal —
62	  recommended, never hard-required.
63	
64	## Structure
65	
66	```
67	skills/local/git-workflow/
68	├── SKILL.md
69	├── scripts/
70	│   ├── branch-status.sh        # classify branches: active/merged/gone/stale
71	│   └── check-commit-msg.sh     # validate header + optional agentic contract
72	├── tests/
73	│   └── test_check_commit_msg.sh
74	├── references/
75	│   ├── project-tiers.md        # main vs dev vs PR + GitHub Flow
76	│   ├── conventional-commits.md # the commit message spec, condensed
77	│   ├── worktrees-parallel-agents.md
78	│   ├── versioning-and-releases.md
79	│   ├── branch-hygiene.md
80	│   └── lazygit-cheatsheet.md   # learning aid
81	└── assets/
82	    ├── commit-template.txt      # git config commit.template
83	    └── worktreeinclude.template # example .worktreeinclude
84	```
85	
86	## Relationship to secret hygiene
87	
88	This skill **defers** all secret scanning and agent-transcript handling to
89	[`agent-history-hygiene`](agent-history-hygiene.md). At commit/merge time it
90	calls that skill's `scan-staged.sh` (exit `0` clean / `10` redacted / `20`
91	leaks) and points at its rotate-first remediation runbook rather than
92	reimplementing any of it. When a project doesn't check agent transcripts in,
93	drop them before a squash-merge; when it does, stage them with that skill.
94	
95	## Cross-harness agentic commits
96	
97	Keep the human as Git author/committer and use one portable final trailer block:
98	
99	```text
100	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
101	
102	Explain why the change was needed, its outcome, and meaningful validation.
103	
104	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
105	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
106	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
107	```
108	
109	Native Claude/Cursor attribution or signing remains additive. The companion
110	`agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh` derives this block from
111	staged artifacts; `check-commit-msg.sh --agentic --staged` validates the full
112	message. Signing is separate and opt-in—this skill never changes Git or harness
113	configuration unless the user explicitly asks.
114	
115	The dated behavior matrix and the distinction between co-author trailers,
116	Cursor line tracking/cloud signatures, and Codex's currently undocumented
117	attribution setting are in
118	[Git workflow best practices](../reference/git-workflow.md#agentic-commit-provenance).
119	
120	## Gotchas
121	
122	- `merge.ff only` refuses a diverged pull on purpose — resolve with
123	  `git pull --rebase`.
124	- A squash-merged branch never shows under `git branch --merged`; it shows as
125	  `gone` upstream. `branch-status.sh` classifies this correctly (delete with
126	  `-D`, after confirming no unpushed work).
127	- Tracked files in `.worktreeinclude` do nothing — it copies **only gitignored**
128	  matches; a committed `.vscode/settings.json` is already in the worktree.
129	- The English-commit rule holds under Chinese prompts — translate the intent,
130	  don't mirror the prompt language into the log.
131	- Commit templates do not affect `git commit -m`, which agent harnesses commonly
132	  use; validate with `check-commit-msg.sh --agentic` instead.
133	- Squash/amend creates a new commit object, so copy canonical trailers into the
134	  squash message and do not amend a vendor-signed commit solely for metadata.
135	
136	## See also
137	
138	- [Source](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/git-workflow)
139	- [Git workflow best practices](../reference/git-workflow.md) — the concepts
140	  explainer (Conventional Commits, SemVer, GitHub Flow, worktrees).
141	- [`agent-history-hygiene`](agent-history-hygiene.md) — secret + transcript
142	  hygiene this skill defers to at commit/merge time.
143
````

21	| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | 「這則 commit message 合法嗎？」 |
22	| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | 「這個操作在 lazygit 怎麼做？」（學習輔助） |
23	
24	想了解這些預設背後的**原因**（概念而非 skill 機制），讀搭配的科普說明：
25	[Git workflow best practices](../reference/git-workflow.md)。
26	
27	## 何時觸發
28	
29	- 「Commit this」/「幫我 commit」/「整理一下 git」/「寫個 commit message」。
30	- 「該開 branch 還是直接 commit 到 main？」/「要開 PR 嗎？」
31	- 「幫平行 agent 設定 worktree」/「把我的 `.env` 帶進 worktree」。
32	- 「怎麼打 tag / 發 release？」/「bump 版本」。
33	- 「我的 local branch 一團亂——哪些做完了？」/「清理 branch」。
34	- 開新 repo，想要一套一致的 commit/branch/release 慣例給自己與 agent 用。
35	
36	## 三個 tier（層級）
37	
38	把繁瑣度 (ceremony) 對應到真實的協作需求；只有在訊號 (signal) 出現時才升級。
39	
40	| Tier | 形狀 | 分支 | 整合 |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| **1 — 個人 / 早期** | 單一 `main` | commit 到 `main`；短命 local branch 可選 | `pull --rebase`、`merge --ff-only` |
43	| **2 — prod/dev 分流** | `main` = 已發布、`dev` = 整合 | feature branch 由 `dev` 切出 | 合併回 `dev`；release 時 ff `dev`→`main` |
44	| **3 — 多人 / 長大的 vibe-coding** | `main` 隨時可部署 | 短命 `feat/…` → PR | PR review/CI → squash-merge |
45	
46	個人 vibe-coding 專案也可以直接跳到 Tier 3：即使只有一個人，PR 就是「ship
47	一個 feature」的分界，也是 CI 跑的地方。
48	
49	## 預設一覽
50	
51	- **Commit**：英文 `type(scope): subject`；非瑣碎 agent commit 加上 why/outcome
52	  body，以及 `AI-Assisted-By`、`Agent-Transcript`、有 plan 時的
53	  `Agent-Plan` trailers。`feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` 觸發 major bump。
54	- **歷史**：線性——`pull.rebase=true`、`merge.ff=only`；嘈雜的 vibe-coding PR
55	  用 squash-merge，整理過的用 rebase-merge。
56	- **Branch**：人工意圖用 `feat/ fix/ chore/ docs/ refactor/ exp/`，agent/vibe
57	  工作用 `agent/…`，Claude worktree 用 `worktree-*`。
58	- **Worktree**：`claude --worktree <name>`；用 `.worktreeinclude`（只限被
59	  gitignore 的檔）把 `.env` 帶進去；把 `.claude/worktrees/` 加進 gitignore。
60	- **Release**：SemVer、annotated 且 `v` 前綴的 tag；若整個專案是 Python
61	  package，讓 git tag 驅動版本 (setuptools-scm / hatch-vcs)。
62	- **Forge CLI**：`gh` (GitHub) / `glab` (GitLab) 在終端機操作 PR——建議使用，
63	  但絕不硬性依賴。
64	
65	## 結構
66	
67	```
68	skills/local/git-workflow/
69	├── SKILL.md
70	├── scripts/
71	│   ├── branch-status.sh        # 分類 branch：active/merged/gone/stale
72	│   └── check-commit-msg.sh     # 驗證標題與可選 agentic contract
73	├── tests/
74	│   └── test_check_commit_msg.sh
75	├── references/
76	│   ├── project-tiers.md        # main vs dev vs PR + GitHub Flow
77	│   ├── conventional-commits.md # commit message 規範精簡版
78	│   ├── worktrees-parallel-agents.md
79	│   ├── versioning-and-releases.md
80	│   ├── branch-hygiene.md
81	│   └── lazygit-cheatsheet.md   # 學習輔助
82	└── assets/
83	    ├── commit-template.txt      # git config commit.template
84	    └── worktreeinclude.template # .worktreeinclude 範例
85	```
86	
87	## 與 secret 衛生 (hygiene) 的關係
88	
89	這個 skill 把所有 secret 掃描與 agent transcript 處理都**交給**
90	[`agent-history-hygiene`](agent-history-hygiene.md)。在 commit/merge 時它呼叫
91	那個 skill 的 `scan-staged.sh`（exit `0` 乾淨 / `10` 已遮蔽 / `20` 有洩漏），
92	並指向其 rotate-first 的補救 runbook，而不自行重造。專案若不把 agent
93	transcript check in，就在 squash-merge 前移除；若有 check in，就用那個 skill
94	去 stage。
95	
96	## 跨 harness 的 agentic commit
97	
98	Human 保持 Git author/committer，所有 harness 使用同一個可攜的 final trailer
99	block：
100	
101	```text
102	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
103	
104	Explain why the change was needed, its outcome, and meaningful validation.
105	
106	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
107	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
108	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
109	```
110	
111	Claude/Cursor 原生 attribution 或 signing 仍可額外保留。搭配的
112	`agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh` 從 staged artifacts
113	產生此區塊；`check-commit-msg.sh --agentic --staged` 驗證完整訊息。Signing
114	是另一層且只在使用者要求時設定，本 skill 不會自行修改 Git/harness config。
115	
116	各 harness 的日期化盤點，以及 co-author trailer、Cursor line tracking/cloud
117	signature、Codex 尚無文件化 attribution 設定之間的差異，見
118	[Git workflow best practices](../reference/git-workflow.md#agentic-commit-provenance)。
119	
120	## Gotchas（陷阱）
121	
122	- `merge.ff only` 會刻意拒絕分歧 (diverged) 的 pull——用 `git pull --rebase`
123	  解決。
124	- 被 squash-merge 的 branch 永遠不會出現在 `git branch --merged`；它會以
125	  upstream `gone` 呈現。`branch-status.sh` 會正確分類（確認沒有未推送
126	  (unpushed) 的工作後用 `-D` 刪）。
127	- `.worktreeinclude` 裡放已追蹤 (tracked) 的檔沒有作用——它只複製被 gitignore
128	  的比對項；已 commit 的 `.vscode/settings.json` 本來就在 worktree 裡。
129	- 英文 commit 規則在中文 prompt 下依然成立——翻譯意圖，不要把 prompt 語言
130	  照抄進歷史。
131	- Agent 常用的 `git commit -m` 不會讀 commit template；要靠
132	  `check-commit-msg.sh --agentic` 驗證。
133	- Squash/amend 會建立新的 commit object；要把 canonical trailers 帶進 squash
134	  message，也不要只為 metadata 去 amend vendor-signed commit。
135	
136	## 另見
137	
138	- [Source](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/git-workflow)

140	  (Conventional Commits、SemVer、GitHub Flow、worktree)。
141	- [`agent-history-hygiene`](agent-history-hygiene.md)——這個 skill 在

2	
3	A concept-level explainer for the conventions the

5	*why* — it's usable on its own as a primer, independent of the skill's scripts.

8

24	
25	## Commit messages: Conventional Commits
26	
27	A commit message is documentation *and* an API for tooling. The
28	[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
29	convention gives each commit a machine-readable prefix:
30	
31	```
32	<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>
33	```
34	
35	Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`,
36	`build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. The subject is a short **imperative** phrase
37	("add retry", not "added retry"), lowercase, no trailing period, ideally ≤ 72
38	characters. A `!` (or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) marks an incompatible change.
39	
40	Why bother when working solo? Because the log becomes a changelog you can
41	generate, a version bump you can compute, and a history you can `git log
42	--grep 'feat'` months later. Write commits in **English** even when you think
43	and prompt in another language — the object graph is read by tools and future
44	collaborators.
45	
46	## Agentic commit provenance
47	
48	Agentic coding adds several signals that are easy to conflate. Keep them as
49	separate layers:
50	
51	| Layer | What it means |
52	|---|---|
53	| Git author / committer | The human or service identity that created the commit object. |
54	| `Co-Authored-By` | Message attribution recognized by hosting UIs; not a signature. |
55	| `AI-Assisted-By` | This workflow's portable harness + model provenance. |
56	| Transcript / plan trailers | Repo-relative links to the detailed review trail committed with the diff. |
57	| SSH/GPG signature | Proof that a key signed the exact commit object. |
58	
59	The portable contract is:
60	
61	```text
62	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
63	
64	Explain why the change was needed, the resulting behavior, and meaningful
65	validation. Agent-produced non-trivial commits always include this body.
66	
67	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
68	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
69	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
70	```
71	
72	Repeat the trailers for multiple agents or artifacts. Keep paths repo-relative
73	and include only files in the same commit. Tool-native attribution is additive,
74	but the canonical fields stay in the **final trailer block**, which is the
75	structure [`git interpret-trailers --parse`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)
76	can query.
77	
78	### Harness behavior observed on 2026-08-27
79	
80	| Harness | Native behavior | Portable-workflow consequence |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| Claude Code | Commit/PR attribution is a configurable runtime feature; its default commit attribution includes a Generated-with line and model-specific `Co-Authored-By`. | Preserve it and append canonical `AI-Assisted-By` + artifact paths. Commit-body quality is a separate agent behavior. |
83	| Cursor | AI commit-message generation uses the staged diff and repository history. Cursor also has line-level AI tracking; Cloud Agent commits are cryptographically signed with an HSM-backed Ed25519 key. | Do not call line attribution, a message trailer, and a Verified commit the same thing. Preserve native signals and add the portable trailers. |
84	| Codex CLI | **Inference:** the official configuration reference reviewed on this date documents no commit-attribution setting. | Use the skill/helper contract instead of inventing an OpenAI co-author email. Re-check upstream docs before claiming this is permanent. |
85	
86	Sources: [Claude Code settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings),
87	[Cursor AI commit messages](https://docs.cursor.com/en/more/ai-commit-message),
88	[Cursor analytics](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/analytics),
89	[Cursor Cloud security](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security), and the
90	[Codex configuration reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/).
91	
92	Squash merges create a new commit. Copy the canonical provenance into the
93	squash message; neither the source commit hash nor its signature survives.
94	Likewise, do not amend a vendor-signed cloud-agent commit solely to add
95	metadata—the amended commit is a different object.
96	
97	## Commit signing
98	
99	Signing is optional and user-owned. This skill never silently changes global
100	Git or agent settings. When the user explicitly asks for SSH signing, inspect
101	their existing config and available public keys, confirm key + scope, then use:
102	
103	```bash
104	git config gpg.format ssh
105	git config user.signingkey /path/to/public-key.pub
106	git config commit.gpgsign true
107	git config tag.gpgsign true       # optional, for signed release tags
108	```
109	
110	With SSH signing, Git accepts a public-key path when the matching private key is
111	available through `ssh-agent`; see [`user.signingKey`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-usersigningKey).
112	The signature authenticates the configured key, while `AI-Assisted-By` records
113	the coding harness/model. One does not replace the other.
114	
115	## Semantic Versioning
116	
117	[SemVer](https://semver.org/) numbers releases `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`:
118	
119	- **MAJOR** — incompatible/breaking changes.
120	- **MINOR** — new, backward-compatible features.
121	- **PATCH** — backward-compatible bug fixes.
122	
123	This maps cleanly onto Conventional Commits: `fix:` → PATCH, `feat:` → MINOR,
124	anything breaking → MAJOR. Below `1.0.0`, anything may change; `1.0.0` is the
125	promise of a stable public interface.
126	
127	## Choosing a workflow by project scale
128	
129	The biggest mistake is applying team ceremony to a solo repo (friction with no
130	benefit) or applying solo habits to a shared repo (collisions, un-reviewable
131	history). Match the workflow to real needs:
132	
133	- **Tier 1 — solo / early.** One `main`. Commit directly, keep history linear
134	  with `git pull --rebase`, land the occasional short-lived branch with
135	  `git merge --ff-only`. No PRs. Tag when a state is worth returning to.
136	- **Tier 2 — prod/dev split.** `main` is the released/deployed line; `dev` is
137	  where features integrate. Promote `dev` → `main` at a release boundary. Adopt
138	  this when something (a deploy, a teammate) depends on a stable line while you
139	  keep working.
140	- **Tier 3 — team / grown vibe-coding.** `main` is always deployable; all work
141	  happens on short-lived branches merged via **pull request** after review and
142	  CI. This is [GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow).
143	  Even a solo project benefits: the PR is a "ship a feature" boundary, a CI
144	  trigger, and a revert point.
145	
146	You can skip tiers — a solo project with heavy CI may start at Tier 3.
147	
148	## Rebase, fast-forward, and squash
149	
150	Three operations shape history:
151	
152	- **`git pull --rebase`** replays your local commits *on top of* the fetched
153	  upstream instead of making a merge commit, keeping history linear. Set it as
154	  the default: `git config pull.rebase true`.
155	- **Fast-forward merge** (`git merge --ff-only`) moves the branch pointer
156	  forward with no merge commit — possible only when there's nothing to
157	  reconcile. `git config merge.ff only` makes git *refuse* a merge that would
158	  create a merge commit, which surfaces divergence instead of hiding it.
159	- **Squash merge** collapses a branch's commits into a single commit on the
160	  target. Ideal for "vibe-coding" branches full of work-in-progress noise: the
161	  mainline gets one clean `feat: …` commit. The trade-off is that the branch's
162	  individual commits don't appear on `main` — so the branch shows as `gone`
163	  rather than `merged` afterward (see [branch hygiene](#branch-naming)).
164	
165	Rule of thumb: linear locally with fast-forward; squash noisy PRs; rebase-merge
166	PRs whose every commit already means something.
167	
168	## Branch naming
169	
170	A `<prefix>/<kebab-description>` convention makes branches sort by intent and
171	lets you clean them up in bulk:
172	
173	- `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `refactor/…`, `exp/…` for
174	  human-authored work (optionally with an issue number: `feat/123-oauth`).
175	- `agent/…` as a distinct namespace for agent / vibe-coding branches, so
176	  machine-generated work is visually separate and separately disposable.
177	- `worktree-*` is what Claude Code auto-creates for worktrees.
178	
179	Keeping these namespaces apart is what makes cleanup (`git branch --list
180	'agent/*'`) safe rather than nerve-wracking. After a PR merges, prune with
181	`git fetch --prune`; a branch whose upstream is `gone` (`git branch -vv`) is
182	usually done — but confirm it has no unpushed commits before deleting, because
183	work sometimes continues on a branch after its PR merged.
184	
185	## Worktrees for parallel work
186	
187	A [git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree) is a second working
188	directory attached to the same repository, on its own branch. Running each
189	parallel agent or task in its own worktree means their file edits never
190	collide. Claude Code integrates this directly
191	([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)):
192	
193	- `claude --worktree <name>` creates `.claude/worktrees/worktree-<name>/` on a
194	  new branch, based on `origin/HEAD` by default.
195	- A worktree is a *fresh* checkout, so gitignored files (like `.env`) aren't
196	  present. A `.worktreeinclude` file at the repo root copies them in — using
197	  `.gitignore` syntax, and copying **only files that are themselves
198	  gitignored**. Already-tracked files (a committed `.vscode/settings.json`) are
199	  in the checkout already and should not be listed.
200	- Add `.claude/worktrees/` to `.gitignore` so worktree contents don't show as
201	  untracked in the main checkout.
202	
203	## Forge CLIs: gh and glab
204	
205	Drive pull/merge requests from the terminal with the platform CLI —
206	[`gh`](https://cli.github.com/) for GitHub, [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli)
207	for GitLab:
208	
209	```bash
210	gh pr create --fill                     # glab mr create --fill
211	gh pr checks                            # watch CI
212	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch    # glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch
213	```
214	
215	They keep you out of the browser for the common path and make PR state
216	scriptable. Treat them as recommended conveniences, not hard dependencies — a
217	good workflow still functions with plain `git` if a CLI is missing.
218	
219	## Tag-driven versioning for packages
220	
221	When a repository *is* a package, don't maintain the version string in three
222	places (`__init__.py`, `pyproject.toml`, and a git tag) and let them drift.
223	Make the **git tag the single source of truth**. For Python, the
224	[Packaging guide](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/)
225	recommends deriving the version from the VCS:
226	
227	- **setuptools** backend → [setuptools-scm](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/).
228	- **Hatch / hatchling** backend → [hatch-vcs](https://pypi.org/project/hatch-vcs/).
229	
230	Tag as `vX.Y.Z` (PEP 440-compatible once the `v` is stripped), push the tag,
231	and the build stamps the matching version. The release process becomes: land
232	the release commit → `git tag -a vX.Y.Z` → push the tag.
233

34	## Agentic commit provenance
35	
36	Agentic coding 帶來幾種很容易混在一起的訊號，應分層理解：
37	
38	| 層次 | 代表意義 |
39	|---|---|
40	| Git author / committer | 建立 commit object 的人類或 service identity。 |
41	| `Co-Authored-By` | Hosting UI 會辨識的 message attribution；不是簽名。 |
42	| `AI-Assisted-By` | 本工作流定義的可攜 harness + model provenance。 |
43	| Transcript / plan trailer | 指向跟 diff 一起 commit 的詳細 review trail。 |
44	| SSH/GPG signature | 證明某把 key 簽過這個精確 commit object。 |
45	
46	可攜 contract：
47	
48	```text
49	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
50	
51	Explain why the change was needed, the resulting behavior, and meaningful
52	validation. Agent-produced non-trivial commits always include this body.
53	
54	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
55	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
56	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
57	```
58	
59	多個 agent 或 artifact 就重複對應 trailer。路徑必須是 repo-relative，且檔案
60	必須真的存在於同一個 commit。工具原生 attribution 可以保留，但 canonical
61	欄位要放在**最後一個 trailer block**，才能由
62	[`git interpret-trailers --parse`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)
63	穩定查詢。
64	
65	### 2026-08-27 的 harness 盤點
66	
67	| Harness | 原生行為 | 對可攜工作流的影響 |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| Claude Code | Commit/PR attribution 是可設定的 runtime 功能；預設 commit attribution 帶 Generated-with 文字與含 model 的 `Co-Authored-By`。 | 保留原生資訊，再加 canonical `AI-Assisted-By` 與 artifact path。Body 品質是另一層 agent 行為。 |
70	| Cursor | AI commit message 會參考 staged diff 與 repo history；另有 line-level AI tracking。Cloud Agent commit 則用 HSM-backed Ed25519 key 做 cryptographic signing。 | Line attribution、message trailer 與 Verified commit 不是同一件事；保留原生訊號並補上可攜 trailers。 |
71	| Codex CLI | **推論：**截至盤點日，官方 configuration reference 沒有記載 commit attribution 設定。 | 使用 skill/helper contract，不虛構 OpenAI co-author email；日後聲稱此限制前要重查 upstream。 |
72	
73	來源：[Claude Code settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)、
74	[Cursor AI commit messages](https://docs.cursor.com/en/more/ai-commit-message)、
75	[Cursor analytics](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/analytics)、
76	[Cursor Cloud security](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security)、
77	[Codex configuration reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/)。
78	
79	Squash merge 會建立新的 commit，因此要把 canonical provenance 複製到 squash
80	message；原 commit hash 與 signature 都不會存活。同理，不要只為了補 metadata
81	而 amend vendor-signed cloud-agent commit——amend 後已是另一個 object。
82	
83	## Commit signing
84	
85	Signing 是 opt-in 且由使用者擁有。Skill 不會默默修改 global Git 或 harness
86	設定。使用者明確要求 SSH signing 時，先檢查現有 config 與 public key、確認 key
87	和 scope，再設定：
88	
89	```bash
90	git config gpg.format ssh
91	git config user.signingkey /path/to/public-key.pub
92	git config commit.gpgsign true
93	git config tag.gpgsign true       # 可選：release tag 也簽名
94	```
95	
96	SSH signing 可在 matching private key 已由 `ssh-agent` 載入時使用 public-key
97	path；詳見 [`user.signingKey`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-usersigningKey)。
98	Signature 驗證 key；`AI-Assisted-By` 記錄 coding harness/model，兩者不能互相取代。
99	
100	## 語意化版本 (Semantic Versioning)
101	
102	[SemVer](https://semver.org/) 用 `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` 標號 release：
103	
104	- **MAJOR**——不相容 / 破壞性 (breaking) 變更。
105	- **MINOR**——新增且向後相容 (backward-compatible) 的功能。
106	- **PATCH**——向後相容的 bug 修復。
107	
108	這乾淨對應到 Conventional Commits：`fix:` → PATCH、`feat:` → MINOR、任何
109	breaking → MAJOR。`1.0.0` 之前一切都可能改；`1.0.0` 是穩定公開介面的承諾。
110	
111	## 依專案規模選工作流
112	
113	最大的錯誤是把團隊的繁瑣度套到個人 repo（只有摩擦沒有好處），或把個人習慣
114	套到共享 repo（衝突、無法審閱的歷史）。把工作流對應到真實需求：
115	
116	- **Tier 1 — 個人 / 早期。** 單一 `main`。直接 commit，用 `git pull --rebase`
117	  保持線性，偶爾用 `git merge --ff-only` 落地短命 branch。不開 PR。值得回頭
118	  的狀態就打 tag。
119	- **Tier 2 — prod/dev 分流。** `main` 是已發布 / 已部署的線；`dev` 是功能整合
120	  的地方。release 時把 `dev` → `main` 升級。當有東西（部署、隊友）依賴穩定線
121	  而你還在開發時採用。
122	- **Tier 3 — 團隊 / 長大的 vibe-coding。** `main` 隨時可部署；所有工作都在
123	  短命 branch 上、經 review 與 CI 後透過 **pull request** 合併。這就是
124	  [GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow)。
125	  即使個人專案也受益：PR 是「ship 一個 feature」的分界、CI 的觸發點、以及
126	  回滾 (revert) 點。
127	
128	你可以跳級——重度 CI 的個人專案可以直接從 Tier 3 起步。
129	
130	## Rebase、fast-forward 與 squash
131	
132	三個操作形塑歷史：
133	
134	- **`git pull --rebase`** 把你的 local commit 重播 (replay) 到抓下來的
135	  upstream *之上*，而非產生 merge commit，讓歷史保持線性。設為預設：
136	  `git config pull.rebase true`。
137	- **快轉合併 (fast-forward merge)**（`git merge --ff-only`）只把 branch 指標
138	  往前移、不產生 merge commit——只有在沒有東西需要調解 (reconcile) 時才可能。
139	  `git config merge.ff only` 讓 git *拒絕*會產生 merge commit 的合併，把分歧
140	  攤開而不是藏起來。
141	- **Squash merge** 把一個 branch 的所有 commit 壓成目標上的單一 commit。很適合
142	  充滿 work-in-progress 雜訊的 vibe-coding branch：主線只拿到一個乾淨的
143	  `feat: …` commit。代價是該 branch 的個別 commit 不會出現在 `main` 上——所以
144	  之後它會顯示為 `gone` 而非 `merged`（見 [Branch 命名](#branch)）。
145	
146	原則：local 用 fast-forward 保持線性；嘈雜的 PR 用 squash；每個 commit 都有
147	意義的 PR 用 rebase-merge。
148	
149	## Branch 命名
150	
151	`<prefix>/<kebab-描述>` 慣例讓 branch 依意圖排序，也讓你能批次清理：
152	
153	- 人工撰寫的工作用 `feat/…`、`fix/…`、`chore/…`、`docs/…`、`refactor/…`、
154	  `exp/…`（可帶 issue 編號：`feat/123-oauth`）。
155	- `agent/…` 作為 agent / vibe-coding branch 的獨立命名空間，讓機器生成的工作
156	  在視覺上分開、也可分開丟棄。
157	- `worktree-*` 是 Claude Code 為 worktree 自動建立的。
158	
159	把這些命名空間分開，才能讓清理（`git branch --list 'agent/*'`）變得安全而非
160	提心吊膽。PR 合併後用 `git fetch --prune` 修剪；upstream 為 `gone` 的 branch
161	（`git branch -vv`）通常已完成——但刪除前先確認沒有未推送 (unpushed) 的
162	commit，因為有時 PR 合併後 branch 上仍會繼續開發。
163	
164	## 用 worktree 平行開發
165	
166	[git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree) 是接到同一個 repository、
167	位於自己 branch 上的第二個工作目錄。讓每個平行 agent 或任務在自己的 worktree
168	裡跑，它們的檔案編輯就永遠不會衝突。Claude Code 直接整合了這個機制
169	（[docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)）：
170	
171	- `claude --worktree <name>` 在新 branch 上建立
172	  `.claude/worktrees/worktree-<name>/`，預設以 `origin/HEAD` 為基底。
173	- worktree 是*全新*的 checkout，所以被 gitignore 的檔（如 `.env`）不會在裡面。
174	  repo 根目錄的 `.worktreeinclude` 檔會把它們複製進來——用 `.gitignore` 語法，
175	  且**只複製本身被 gitignore 的檔**。已追蹤 (tracked) 的檔（已 commit 的
176	  `.vscode/settings.json`）本來就在 checkout 裡，不該列進去。
177	- 把 `.claude/worktrees/` 加進 `.gitignore`，worktree 內容才不會在主 checkout
178	  顯示為未追蹤 (untracked)。
179	
180	## Forge CLI：gh 與 glab
181	
182	用平台 CLI 在終端機操作 pull/merge request——GitHub 用
183	[`gh`](https://cli.github.com/)、GitLab 用
184	[`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli)：
185	
186	```bash
187	gh pr create --fill                     # glab mr create --fill
188	gh pr checks                            # 看 CI
189	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch    # glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch
190	```
191	
192	它們讓你在常見流程中不必開瀏覽器，也讓 PR 狀態可腳本化 (scriptable)。把它們
193	當作建議的便利工具，而非硬性依賴——即使少了 CLI，好的工作流用純 `git` 仍能
194	運作。
195	
196	## 套件的 tag 驅動版本
197	
198	當一個 repository 本身*就是*一個套件時，別把版本字串維護在三個地方
199	（`__init__.py`、`pyproject.toml`、以及 git tag）任其漂移 (drift)。讓 **git
200	tag 成為單一事實來源 (single source of truth)**。Python 方面，
201	[Packaging 指南](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/)
202	建議由 VCS 推導版本：
203	
204	- **setuptools** backend → [setuptools-scm](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/)。
205	- **Hatch / hatchling** backend → [hatch-vcs](https://pypi.org/project/hatch-vcs/)。
206	
207	以 `vX.Y.Z` 打 tag（去掉 `v` 後需與 PEP 440 相容），推送 tag，build 就會蓋上
208	對應的版本。release 流程變成：落地 release commit → `git tag -a vX.Y.Z` →
209	推送 tag。
210	
211	## 來源
212	
213	- [Conventional Commits v1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
214	- [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/)
215	- [GitHub Flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow)
216	- [Claude Code worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)
217	- [git-worktree docs](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)
218	- [Python Packaging — single-sourcing the version](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/)
219	- [setuptools-scm](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/) ·
220	  [hatch-vcs](https://pypi.org/project/hatch-vcs/)
221
